units.la: CAPUT DECIMUM, CONFESSIONIS HELVETICÆ, De Prædestinatione Dei, & Electione Sanctorum.
units.tr: CHAPTER TEN, OF THE CONFESSION OF HELVETIA: Concerning the Predestination of God and the Election of the Saints.

units.la: DEus ab æterno prædestinavit, vel elegit liberè & merâ suâ gratiâ, nullo hominum respectu, sanctos, quos vult salvos facere in Christo, juxta illud Apostoli: a Deus elegit nos in ipso, antequam jacerentur fundamenta mundi. Et iterum, b qui salvos fecit nos, & vocavit vocatione sanctâ, non secundum opera nostra; sed secundum suum propositum, & gratiam, quæ data quidem est nobis, per Christum Jesum, ante tempora æterna; sed palàm facta est, nunc per apparitionem Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi.
units.tr: God from eternity predestined, or chose, freely and by his mere grace, without any regard to men, the saints whom he wills to save in Christ, according to that saying of the Apostle: a God chose us in him before the foundation of the world. And again: b who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before eternal times, but has now been made manifest through the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ.

units.la: Ergo non sine medio, licet non propter ullum meritum nostrum; sed in Christo, & propter Christum, nos elegit Deus, ut, qui jam sunt in Christo insiti per fidem, illi etiam ipsi sint electi; reprobi verò, qui sunt extra Christum, secundum illud Apostoli: c Vos ipsos tentate, num sitis in fide. An non agnoscitis vosmet ipsos, quod Jesus Christus in vobis est? nisi forte reprobi estis.
units.tr: Therefore God chose us, not without a means, though not on account of any merit of ours, but in Christ and for Christ's sake, so that those who are already grafted into Christ through faith should themselves also be elect; while the reprobate are those who are outside Christ, according to that saying of the Apostle: c Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith. Do you not recognise yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless perhaps you are reprobate.

units.la: Denique; electi sunt sancti in Christo, per Deum, ad finem certum, quem & ipsum exponit Apostolus, & ait: d Elegit nos in ipso, ut essemus sancti, & irreprehensibiles coram illo per charitatem. Qui prædestinavit nos, ut adoptaret in filios, per Jesum Christum, in sese, ut laudetur gloria gratiæ suæ.
units.tr: Finally, the saints are elect in Christ, by God, to a certain end, which the Apostle himself sets forth, saying: d He chose us in him, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love. He predestined us to adopt us as sons through Jesus Christ, unto himself, to the praise of the glory of his grace.

units.la: Et quamvis e Deus nôrit, qui sint sui; Et alicubi mentio fiat f paucitatis electorum; bene sperandum est tamen de omnibus, neque temerè reprobis quisquam est annumerandus. Paulus certè ad Philip-
units.tr: And although e God knows who are his own; and although mention is made somewhere of f the fewness of the elect; yet we ought to hope well of all, and no one is to be rashly counted among the reprobate. Paul certainly, writing to the Philippians,

units.la: a Ephes.1: 3.4. b.2.Tim, 1:9.10, c 2.Cor, 13:5. d.Ephes. 1:4.5, e.2.Timoth.2; 19. f Matth. 20:16, 22:14. penf. § Gratias ago, inquit, pro omnibus vobis (loquitur autem de tota Ecclesia Philippensi) quod veneritis in communionem Evangelii, persuasum habens, quod is, qui coepit opus bonum in vobis, perficiet, sicuti justum est, ut hoc sententiam[?] de vobis omnibus. Et cum {h}Luc. 13. rogaretur Dominus an pauci sint, qui salventur: non respondet Dominus ac dicit, paucos, aut plures fore servandos, aut perdendos; sed hortatur potius, ut quisque contendat ingredi per portam arctam. Quasi dixerit; Vestrum non est de his curiosius inquirere; sed magis anniti, ut per rectam viam coelum ingrediamini.
units.tr: a Ephes. 1:3, 4. b 2 Tim. 1:9, 10. c 2 Cor. 13:5. d Ephes. 1:4, 5. e 2 Tim. 2:19. f Matth. 20:16, 22:14. Penult. § I give thanks, he says, for all of you (he speaks of the whole Philippian Church) that you have come into fellowship in the Gospel, being persuaded that he who began a good work in you will complete it, just as it is right that I should think this of you all. And when the Lord was asked whether few are saved (Luke 13), the Lord does not answer that few or many will be saved or lost, but rather exhorts each to strive to enter by the narrow gate. As if he had said: It is not for you to inquire too curiously into these matters; rather strive that you may enter heaven by the right way.

units.la: § 5. Proinde non probamus impias quorundam voces, qui dicunt: Pauci sunt electi, &, cum mihi non constet, an sim in illo paucorum numero, genium meum non fraudabo. Alii dicunt; Si prædestinatus vel electus sum a Deo, nihil impediet me a salute certo jam definita, quicquid tandem designavero. Si vero sum de reproborum numero, nulla me vel fides, vel pœnitentia juvabit; cum definitio Dei mutari non possit. Itaque inutiles sunt doctrinæ, & admonitiones omnes. Nam contra hos pugnat illud Apostoli: {i}Oportet servum Domini propensum esse ad docendum, erudientem eos, qui obsistunt, si quando det Deus illis pœnitentiam, ad cognoscendam veritatem, ut resipiscant a laqueo diaboli, capti ab eo, ad ejus voluntatem.
units.tr: § 5. Accordingly we do not approve of the impious utterances of some, who say: "Few are elect," and, "since I am not sure whether I am in that small number, I will not cheat my own nature." Others say: "If I am predestined or elected by God, nothing will hinder me from salvation, already certainly settled, whatever I may do. But if I am of the number of the reprobate, neither faith nor repentance will help me, since the decree of God cannot be changed. Therefore all doctrines and admonitions are useless." For against these men stands that saying of the Apostle: The servant of the Lord must be gentle towards all, apt to teach, patient, correcting with gentleness those who oppose him, if perhaps God may grant them repentance to the knowledge of the truth, that they may come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his will.

units.la: § 6. Sed & Augustinus de bono perseverantiæ cap. 14. & consequentibus ostendit, utrumque esse prædicandum, & liberæ electionis prædestinationisque gratiam, & admonitiones, & doctrinas salutares.
units.tr: § 6. But Augustine too, in On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 14 and following, shows that both must be preached: both the grace of free election and predestination, and the admonitions and salutary teachings.

units.la: § 7. Improbamus itaque illos, qui extra Christum quærunt; An sint ab æterno electi? Et quid ante omnem æternitatem de ipsis statuerit Deus? Audienda enim est prædicatio Evangelii, eique credendum est, & pro indubitato habendum, si credis, ac sis in Christo, electum te esse. Pater enim prædestinationis suæ æternam sententiam, sicut modo ex Apostolo {k}2. Timoth. 1 :exposuimus; nobis in Christo aperuit.
units.tr: § 7. Therefore we disapprove of those who inquire outside Christ: whether they were elect from eternity, and what God determined concerning them before all eternity. For the preaching of the Gospel is to be heard, and it is to be believed and held as beyond doubt that, if you believe and are in Christ, you are elect. For the Father has revealed to us in Christ the eternal decree of his predestination, as we have just set forth from the Apostle, 2 Timothy 1.

units.la: § 8. Docendum ergo & considerandum ante omnia, quantus amor Patris erga nos in Christo nobis sit revelatus: audiendum quid nobis quotidie ipse in Evangelio. Dominus prædicet, quomodo vocet, & dicat: {l}Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis, & onerati estis, ego vos reficiam.
units.tr: § 8. Therefore, before all things, one must teach and consider how great the Father's love towards us has been revealed to us in Christ; let us hear what the Lord himself daily proclaims in the Gospel, how he calls and says: Come to me, all you who labour and are burdened, and I will refresh you.

units.la: {l} Matth.11.28. [?]iam.[?] {m}Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Unigenitum dederit pro mundo, ut omnis, qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Item: Non est voluntas patris, ut quisquam de his pusillis pereat.
units.tr: {l} Matth. 11:28. [unclear] {m} God so loved the world that he gave his only Son for the world, that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. Likewise: It is not the will of the Father that any of these little ones should perish.

units.la: § 9. Christus itaque sit speculum, in quo prædestinationem nostram contemplemur. Satis perspicuum & firmum habebimus testimonium, nos in libro vitæ inscriptos esse, si communicaverimus cum Christo, & is in vera fide noster sit, nos ejus simus.
units.tr: § 9. Let Christ therefore be the mirror in which we contemplate our predestination. We shall have a sufficiently clear and firm testimony that we are written in the book of life if we have communion with Christ, and if he is ours in true faith, we are his.

units.la: § 10. Consoletur nos in tentatione prædestinationis, quâ vix alia est periculosior, quòd promissiones Dei sunt universales fidelibus, quod ipse ait: {o}Petite, & accipietis. Omnis qui petit accipit. Quòd denique cum universa Dei Ecclesia oramus, Pater noster, qui es in cœlis: & quòd baptismo sumus insiti corpori Christi, & pascimur in Ecclesia ejus carne, & sanguine frequenter ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: § 10. Let us be consoled in the temptation concerning predestination, than which there is hardly any more dangerous, by the fact that the promises of God are universal to believers, as he himself says: Ask, and you will receive. Everyone who asks receives. And finally, by the fact that we pray together with the whole Church of God, "Our Father, who art in heaven"; and that we have been grafted by baptism into the body of Christ, and are frequently fed in his Church with his flesh and blood, unto eternal life.

units.la: § 11. His confirmati {p}cum timore, & tremore, juxta Præceptum Pauli, nostram salutem operari jubemur.
units.tr: § 11. Strengthened by these things, we are commanded, with fear and trembling, according to the precept of Paul, to work out our salvation.

units.la: OECONOMIA TOTIUS CAPITIS.
units.tr: The Economy of the Whole Chapter

units.la: Confessio Helvetica, hoc capite agit de Prædestinatione, h.e.universa, & summariâ salutis humanæ Oeconomiâ, quâ male explicatâ non parum salus nostra perturbatur; rectè autem explicatâ, veræ fiduciæ, humilitati, & gratitudini generandæ unicè inservit.
units.tr: The Helvetic Confession in this chapter treats of predestination, that is, of the whole and summary economy of human salvation. When this is badly explained, our salvation is not a little disturbed; when it is rightly explained, it serves only to produce true confidence, humility and gratitude.

units.la: Explicat autem prædestinationem,
units.tr: It explains predestination as follows:

units.la: I. A distributione tacitâ; sed emphaticâ, in Electionem, & Reprobationem. § 2.
units.tr: I. By a tacit but emphatic distribution into election and reprobation. § 2.

units.la: II. Electionem speciatim explicat. 1. ab adjunctâ æternitate 2. à causa seu fundamento (a) θετικῶς per assertionem; quod est εὐδοκία. (b) ἀντιθετικῶς per rejectionem, quod non fit meritum. § 1. § 3.[?] à fine, quæ est sanctitas. § 3. (4) ab adjuncto numero indefinito, seu (ut Scholæ barbarè loquuntur) quantitate discretâ. Unde (α) nostrum officium, & modestiam in judicando de reprobis colligit, idque probat exemplo Pauli; (β) Curiositati de certo electorum numero investigando occurrit, exemplo Christi § 4.
units.tr: II. It explains election in particular: 1. by its attached eternity; 2. by its cause or foundation: (a) positively, through assertion, which is good pleasure [εὐδοκία]; (b) antithetically, through rejection, which does not become merit. § 1. § 3.[?] 3. by its end, which is holiness. § 3. 4. by its attached indefinite number, or (as the schools barbarously put it) discrete quantity. Hence (α) it draws our duty and modesty in judging the reprobate, and proves this by the example of Paul; (β) it meets the curiosity of inquiring into the certain number of the elect, by the example of Christ. § 4.

units.la: III. Diabolica & impia impiorum argumenta rejicit. 1. testimonio Scripturæ § 1. 2. Augustini. § 6.
units.tr: III. It rejects the diabolical and impious arguments of the impious: 1. by the testimony of Scripture, § 1; 2. by that of Augustine, § 6.

units.la: IV. Ex præmissis, quæstiones curiosas rejicit, & ad audiitionem verbi hortatur, officia præscribendo. 1. generaliter omnibus, § 7. 2. specialiter. α, Ministris. β, Auditoribus § 8.
units.tr: IV. From what has been premised, it rejects curious questions and urges people to hear the Word, prescribing duties: 1. generally, to all, § 7; 2. specifically: α, to ministers; β, to hearers, § 8.

units.la: I. Prædestinatio, peculiare Dei circa creaturas intelligentes consilium, teste Calvino, communis fuit omnium ab initio errantium scopulus. Unde à multis perperam modestis, omnis ejus mentio, æterno oblivionis cinere sepulta jaceri volebat, imò ut Deo, & Scripturæ injuriosis, caliginis nomen obtinebat. Quod sanè mirum non debet videri. Si quidem oportet eos, qui sine luce scripturæ, in tanto arcano explicando, propriis indulgentes hariolationibus, procedere conantur, ut cæcutirent; ita in illum incidere labyrinthum, cujus nullum reperiant exitum. Quod idem nobis facile contingere potuisset, nisi nostra, qualiacunque tandem illa sint, ex Scriptura, & Confessione Helvetica, unicè ex Scripturis petita, luci proseminaremus. Doctorum scripta, ut minimè contemnimus: ita ad credulam spei perplexæ auram, non ubique antennas solvimus; Sed sine ullo rubore, ubi balbutiendum est, cum scriptura balbutiemus, ubi quid determinandum, subsistemus, ut animum advertamus, & lecta cum aliis Dei verbis conferamus; putamus enim Deum in hoc etiam arcano suo, benignè nobiscum in scripturis egisse, & se, pro sua sapientia, ad captum nostrum accommodâsse.
units.tr: I. Predestination, the peculiar counsel of God concerning intelligent creatures, was, as Calvin testifies, the rock on which all who have erred from the beginning have been wrecked. Hence many, though with modest intentions, have wished every mention of it buried in the eternal ashes of oblivion, and it has even gained, as something injurious to God and Scripture, the name of darkness. This indeed ought not to seem surprising. For those who, without the light of Scripture, and indulging their own guesses, try to proceed in explaining so great a mystery, must necessarily grope about blindly, and so fall into that labyrinth from which they find no exit. The same might easily have happened to us, had we not brought our own views, however they may be, into the light from Scripture and the Helvetic Confession, drawn solely from the Scriptures. We do not despise the writings of the teachers, yet we do not everywhere loose our sails to the credulous breeze of an anxious hope. Rather, without any blush, where we must stammer, we stammer with Scripture; where something must be determined, we stand firm; and we attend to and compare what we have read with the other words of God. For we think that God, in this mystery too, has dealt kindly with us in the Scriptures, and has, in his wisdom, accommodated himself to our capacity.

units.la: II. Quare primò prædestinationis doctrinam simul in existentiam ejus inquirentes in Ecclesia Dei docendam esse demonstrabimus. Tandem Methodo Historicâ Confessioni Helveticæ propriâ, nobis verò familiari, pro illa, quæ nobis à Domino communicata est, gratiæ mensurâ, ipsam Confessionem syncerè, & ad conscientiam explicare conabimur. Quam nostram intentionem frigidi, & charitatis expertes, si non laudabunt, saltem factum, ut speramus, non vituperabunt.
units.tr: II. Therefore, first, we will show that the doctrine of predestination is to be taught in the Church of God together with an inquiry into its existence. Lastly, by the historical method proper to the Helvetic Confession, yet familiar to us, and according to the measure of grace that the Lord has granted us, we shall try to explain the Confession itself sincerely and in a way that speaks to the conscience. If the cold and those without charity do not praise this intention of ours, at least, as we hope, they will not find fault with the deed.

units.la: III. Nimia sanè Doctorum fuit illa verecundia, quâ, prout Prophetias semper obscuras clamitabant: itâ doctrinam Prædestinationis explicandam fugiebant. Nos certè longè aliter sumus animati, quàm ut cum illis accusemus prophetiarum propter parabolas, & ænigmata intermixta, prædestinationis, propter altitudinem sapientiæ, & cognitionis Dei, obscuritatem, & putemus, nisi Elias ἑρμηνεύς, interpres, cœlô missus descendat, ea intelligi non posse. Imò ut omnem scripturam: ita etiam eam ejus partem, quæ prædestinationis augustum præ se fert titulum, sobriè & sine præjudiciis, explicandam, & tutò proponendam, hoc solùm unico argumento judicamus: Quia Apostolus, Doctor in cœlesti Academia creatus, ferè hoc in omnibus agit Epistolis, ut ostendat salutem nostram non esse rem novam, &c ἐκμεταμελείας ac sero consilio constitutam ; sed ipsa etiam fundatione terræ antiquiorem, & ab æterno τετυπωμένην, designatam. Et certè ii, qui nos volunt raro de ea dicere, raro etiam nos volunt de ea cogitare, raro ejus pignus requirere, raro gratias Deo pro ea agere ; atque omninò amorem Dei in cordibus nostris effusum, parum serio, & sedulò meditari.
units.tr: III. That reverence of the teachers was surely excessive, by which, just as they always cried that the prophecies were obscure, so they shunned explaining the doctrine of predestination. We are certainly minded far otherwise than to accuse the prophecies with them, because of the parables and enigmas mixed in, and to accuse predestination, because of the depth of wisdom and the obscurity of the knowledge of God, and to think it cannot be understood unless Elijah, the interpreter [ἑρμηνεύς], is sent down from heaven. Indeed, as we judge every Scripture, so also that part of it which bears the august title of predestination is to be explained soberly and without prejudice, and set forth safely, on this single argument alone: the Apostle, a teacher created in the heavenly academy, does this in almost all his Epistles, to show that our salvation is not a new matter, nor established as an afterthought [ἐκμεταμελείας] and by a late counsel, but is older even than the foundation of the earth, and was from eternity prefigured and designed [τετυπωμένην]. And certainly those who want us to speak of it rarely, want us also to think of it rarely, to seek its pledge rarely, to give thanks to God for it rarely; and altogether they want us to meditate on the love of God poured out in our hearts to little purpose and with little seriousness.

units.la: IV. Blasphemè igitur, & injuriosè, clarissima illa Scripturæ Lux, & lucidus Sol, in cordis nostri lucens hemisphærio, à cœcis, illum intueri non valentibus, caliginis & tenebrarum honore damnatus est ; Unica enim nostra electio est lux illa, quæ nobis, ut nautis nocturnâ caligine labantibus, in mari hoc mundo à Deo alieno, ventis, & agitationibus Principis hujus sæculi subjecto, undis nigrescentibus tumido, fluctibus suis, ipsam cœli, & Ecclesiæ faciem hostiliter, & seditiosè invadentibus, faces rutilas suppeditat. Unica nostra electio, est Lûna illa splendida, quæ, in perpetua hujus mundi nocte, recreationem, & solatium præbet, quæ mundum hunc, palpabilibus tenebris plenum, luce suâ distinguit, & jucundiorem facit. Sit ergo aliis à Deo hujus mundi occæcatis caligo, nobis tamen lux & Solis fulgor erit, sit tenebræ, sed eæ, ex quibus jussit Deus, ut lux, h.e. gloria ejus, & salus nostra, exsplendescerent.
units.tr: IV. Blasphemously and injuriously, therefore, that most clear light of Scripture, the bright sun shining in the hemisphere of our heart, has been condemned to the honour of darkness and shadow by the blind, who cannot look upon it. For our election is that one light which, like a sailor wavering in the night's darkness on a sea alien to God, subject to the winds and agitations of the prince of this age, swollen with blackening waves whose surges hostilely and seditiously invade the very face of heaven and of the Church, supplies us with ruddy torches. Our one election is that splendid moon which, in the perpetual night of this world, offers refreshment and solace, which distinguishes this world, full of tangible darkness, by its light, and makes it more pleasant. Let there be darkness for others, blinded by the god of this world; for us it will be light and the splendour of the sun. Let there be shadows, but shadows out of which God commanded light to shine forth, that is, his glory and our salvation.

units.la: V. Fatemur hîc esse imperscrutabilia Dei judicia, altitudinem sapientiæ & cognitionis ejus ; sed pari etiam jure agnoscimus, divitiarum ejus profunditatem, non certè per tenacitatem conclusarum, (quasi Deus ut avarus aliquis, & non ingenuus, munificus, divitiis suis incubaret tantùm, & eas nulli distribueret, ) sed per liberalitatem in cordibus nostris effusarum. Agnoscimus, prædestinationem, adeoque electionem esse viam Dei, eámque rectam, quam prudentes, & considerantes, ut ex Scriptura intelligunt : ita in ea, & secundùm eam ambulant, quamvis improbi eam non intelligant ; sed improbè agant, & tanquam defectores in eam impingant.
units.tr: V. We confess that there are unsearchable judgments of God here, and the depth of his wisdom and knowledge. But by the same right we acknowledge the depth of his riches. This is not by the tightness of stores kept shut (as if God, like some miserly and ungenerous man, brooded over his riches alone and distributed them to no one), but by the liberality poured out in our hearts. We acknowledge that predestination, and so election, is the way of God, and a right one, which the prudent and thoughtful understand from Scripture and therefore walk in it and according to it, although the wicked do not understand it, but act wickedly and, as apostates, stumble upon it.

units.la: VI. Intrepidè igitur vestigiis scripturæ insistemus, & in existentiam æternæ prædestinationis hoc modo inquiremus. Ponimus γνωστὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος εἶναι τῷ Θεῷ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ h.e. habuisse Deum ab æterno decretum & consilium, non tantùm prout illud est origo, & causa omnium rerum, & omnibus rebus perid constitutus est finis, neque quatenus circa peccata æquè, ac bona versatur ; sed etiam in quantum est causa dispensationis gratiæ & iræ, quod ultimum probatum imus. Primò Scripturæ locis Ephes. 1.4. 2.Tim.1.9. 1.Thess. 5.9. 2.Tim.2.19 Luc.10.20. Eph.1.11. Rom.11.
units.tr: VI. Fearlessly, therefore, we will follow the footsteps of Scripture, and in this way inquire into the existence of eternal predestination. We lay down that all his works are known to God from eternity [γνωστὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος εἶναι τῷ Θεῷ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ]; that is, that God had from eternity a decree and counsel, not only as it is the origin and cause of all things, and by which an end is appointed for all things, nor only insofar as it is equally concerned with sins and with goods, but also insofar as it is the cause of the dispensation of grace and of wrath; and this last we will prove. First, from the passages of Scripture: Eph. 1.4; 2 Tim. 1.9; 1 Thess. 5.9; 2 Tim. 2.19; Luke 10.20; Eph. 1.11; Rom. 11.

units.la: 2. Præprimis autem ex Epistola sancti Pauli ad Rom. capite nono, v.22.23. Θέλων ὁ Θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν, καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ, ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς, κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν· καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν; Deus volens ostendere i-ram, & notam facere potentiam suam, tulit in multa longanimitate vasa ira aptata ad interitum; & ut notas faceret divitias gloriae suae in vasa misericordiae, quae praeparavit ad gloriam. Ubi consilium irae,& gratiae exercendae ex eo asseritur,quòd sint quidam ex Israële,ut vasa irae ad interitum exaptata,ad hoc posita,ut Deus in ipsis iram suam demonstraret:quidam vero,ut vasa misericordiae praeparata ad gloriam,ad hoc posita,ut in ipsis notas faceret divitias gloriae suae. Hoc volunt, Syrus,&Arabs.
units.tr: 2. Especially from the Epistle of St Paul to the Romans, chapter nine, verses 22 and 23: What if God, willing to show his wrath and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering vessels of wrath fitted for destruction; and that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he had prepared beforehand for glory? [Θέλων ὁ Θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν, καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ, ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς, κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν· καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους, ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν]. Here the counsel of exercising wrath and grace is asserted from this: that some from Israel, as vessels of wrath fitted for destruction, were set there so that God might display his wrath in them; while others, as vessels of mercy prepared for glory, were set there so that he might make known the riches of his glory in them. The Syriac and Arabic versions hold this view.

units.la: Fuit,cum voluisset Deus ostendere iram,& manifestare quantum ea valeat;protulit (volens in praesentiam accersivit,coràm accersi jussit,quod Radix [?]حضر in X.conjugatione emphaticè significat) cum multa longanimitate (expectatione) vasa irae apparata ad interitum. Et ut manifestaret numerositatem gloriae suae ampla erga vasa misericordiae, quae preparaverat (Arabs,uti ipsi in similibus solenne est,verbum [?]προῳλοίμασεν vocibus duabus exprimit [?]سبق praecessit,praecurrit & [illegible, ~4 letters] quae in Conj. X. notat dispositum & paratum esse) ad gloriam. Secundo. Ex ipsa differenti gratiae dispensatione,tanquam optimo decreti Dei [?]ἐρμηνεί surgimus ad consilium gratiae,& irae exercendae aeternum. Sic argumentantes: Gratia Dei in tempore in certos quosdam homines fertur,& non in omnes. Ergo consilium Dei fuit ab aeterno gratiam suam cum certis quibusdam hominibus exercendi,& iram justam,cum aliis,qui scil. à gratiae communione sunt exclusi. Quod amplius demonstrare pergimus. Nempe Vocatio efficax, prima aeterni Dei amoris in cordibus nostris effusio,h.e. primum illud, quod constituit hominem in sese electum; non est universalis: Nam [?]משה
units.tr: It was when God willed to show his wrath and to make plain how far it prevails that he brought forward (the Arabic verb, which in the tenth form means "to summon into his presence, to order to be brought before him," is here rendered as "brought forward") with much long-suffering (that is, with patient waiting) the vessels of wrath made ready for destruction. And so that he might show the abundance of his glory toward the vessels of mercy which he had prepared (the Arabic renders the Greek verb proētoimasen with two words, sabaqa, "went before, ran ahead," and a further word which in the tenth form means "arranged and made ready") for glory. Second. From this very difference in the dispensation of grace, as from the best interpreter of God's decree, we rise to the eternal purpose of exercising grace and wrath. We argue thus: the grace of God in time is bestowed on certain men and not on all. Therefore God's purpose from eternity was to exercise his grace towards certain men and his just wrath towards others, namely those who are excluded from fellowship in grace. We go on to show this more fully. Namely, effectual calling, the first outpouring of the eternal love of God into our hearts, that is, the first thing which makes a man elect in himself, is not universal. For the [Hebrew: mishah] ... rod, measuring line of foundation ...

units.la: pirum [?] patrum subjugationis, nequidem in nova Ecclesiae administratione, omnem metitur transitum h. e. Praedicatio Evangelii, tanquam pertica designans fundationis, h. e. Ecclesiae limites, super omni loco, cum tympanis, & citharis, ad maximas istas nuptias invitantibus, non requiescit, neque ad totum mare, & desertum hactenus pertigit, quia mare totum nondum f. stat terra, neque omne desertum frugifera. Non ut igitur efficaciter omnes vocarentur; sed quoad ipsam externam etiam verbi promulgationem, multos oportet esse extraneos Iustificatio, sententia illa Dei gratiosa, quâ propter Christum fide apprehensum absolvitur fidelis à peccato, & morte, & justus ad vitam reputatur, eorum tantum est, qui verâ in Christum fide donantur, aliis revelata est ira Dei de coelis, quae eos, ut vas figuli dissilire facit. Adoptio, ut & Sanctificatio, & glorificatio est eorum, tantum qui efficaciter vocantur, & justificantur, adeoque non est omnium. Non enim Deus dat omnibus ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γίνεσθαι, utpote iis qui manent filii degeneres, defectores corrumpentes בנים מרעים משחיתים. Non omnes sanctificantur, quia plures in vilitate luti relinquuntur, quam gypso ornantur. Neque omnes glorificantur, quia ut ab animali vita ad spiritualem in tempore non transferuntur; ita neque ex terra in coelestem Hyerusalem exaltabuntur, ut à miseria, & aeterna peccati poena in aeternam felicitatem transmutarentur. Certissimum est Deum, in iis, quos glorificat, ut in thesauro סגלה, & peculio suo, quo se ostenter, quod non prodigat, gloriari, deliciari. At quàm multi sunt in quibus nulla est ejus delectatio? quàm multi sunt surculi abominabiles נצרים נתעבים, veneno, & absynthio fructificantes, qui ut radices venenatae, & noxiae arboris, non conduntur in terra Dei, id est, Ecclesia, neque plantantur, ut crescant; sed projiciuntur ut exarescant. Ex quâ manifestâ dispensationis gratiae quoad homines differentiâ, pro certo concludimus, Deum quosdam ab aeterno ordinâsse ad hoc, ut consilium gratiae exercendae, in iis, in tempore exerceat, quia eis offert gratiae primitias; quosdam ad hoc, ut consilium irae exercendae in iis manifestet, eo quòd in tempore eos negligat. Quod consilium irae & gratiae exercendae, uno nomine, vulgò Praedestinationem h. e. electionem, & reprobationem, vocamus.
units.tr: ... of the fathers' subjugation. Not even in the new administration of the Church does the preaching of the gospel measure every passage, as a measuring line marking out the foundation, that is, the limits of the Church. It does not rest over every place, inviting with timbrels and harps to those great nuptials, nor has it yet reached the whole sea and desert, because the whole sea is not yet made firm land, nor is every desert fruitful. Therefore, not all are called effectually; and even as to the external proclamation of the word itself, many must be strangers. Justification, that gracious sentence of God by which, on account of Christ apprehended by faith, the believer is absolved from sin and death and reckoned righteous to life, belongs only to those who are granted it through true faith in Christ; for others the wrath of God is revealed from heaven, which makes them shatter like a potter's vessel. Adoption, as also sanctification and glorification, belongs only to those who are effectually called and justified, and so is not for all. For God does not give to all the power to become children of God [exousian tekna theou ginesthai], since they remain degenerate sons, corrupting deserters [banim mera'im mashchitim]. Not all are sanctified, because more are left in the vileness of mud than are adorned with gypsum. Nor are all glorified; for just as they are not transferred in time from animal life to spiritual life, so neither will they be raised from the earth to the heavenly Jerusalem, to be changed from misery and the eternal punishment of sin into eternal happiness. It is most certain that God glories and delights in those whom he glorifies, as in a treasure [segullah] and his own special possession, in which he shows himself, and which he does not squander. But how many are there in whom he takes no delight? How many are abominable shoots [netsarim ne'eavim], bearing fruit of poison and wormwood, which, like the roots of a poisonous and harmful tree, are not stored in God's land, that is, the Church, nor planted to grow, but are cast out to wither! From this plain difference in the dispensation of grace among men, we firmly conclude that God has from eternity ordained some to this end: that he exercise in them, in time, the purpose of exercising grace, since he offers them the first fruits of grace; and others to this end: that he show in them the purpose of exercising wrath, because he neglects them in time. This twofold purpose of exercising wrath and grace we commonly call, in one word, predestination, that is, election and reprobation.

units.la: VII. Nec male, quamvis enim Scriptura, utatur potius eo vocabulo, quando designat, ordinationem, & definitionem certorum hominum, ad hoc bonum, ut in iis manifestetur gratia Dei gloriosa Eph. 1:4. f. 6. Rom. 8:29 30. tamen quia in utraque parte hujus consilii fit ὁρισμὸς definitio, & προορισμὸς Praedefinitio, versans circa actiones etiam eorum, qui pereunt Luc. 22:22. Act. 4:24. rectissime ad speciale hoc decretum indigitandum, cum Theologis Reformatis adhibemus.
units.tr: VII. Nor is this wrongly done. Although Scripture prefers the term when it designates the ordaining and defining of certain men to this good end, that in them the glorious grace of God may be shown (Eph. 1:4; Eph. 6; Rom. 8:29-30), yet because in both parts of this purpose there is horismos, definition, and proorismos, predefinition, which concerns even the actions of those who perish (Luke 22:22; Acts 4:24), we rightly use, together with the Reformed theologians, this word to designate this special decree.

units.la: VIII. Neque obstat Confessio, quae videtur Praedestinationem sumere[?] pro electione tantum, exclusa reprobatione, dum §. 1. exegetice dicit, Deus ab aterno praedestinavit, vel elegit sanctos; Usum enim vocis hujus (ut statim dictum est) Confessio, ut ex Scriptura didicit: ita retinere, & cum ea loqui voluit. Vulgarem, notum, & communem omnibus suppositi, generale speciei accommodavit, h.e. quod erat indefinitum, indeterminatum, id definivit, & determinavit. Amplius, Confessio, non urget Scholasticam illam, & Babylonicam methodum, qua nostrum (proh dolor!) caecutit saeculum, & merito, ut ad rem tanti momenti indagandam ineptam, subtilem magis; quam veram, sed pergit methodo Sp. Sancti, in Scriptura loquentis, quam unicam primi Evangelii restauratores, utpote utilem, religiose sequuti sunt. Et quia ea methodus, unica, vera est, & Dei est, adeoque illa incesserunt, teste toto mundo felicius nobis processerunt, siquidem vel minimum, quod a Deo est, & Dei est, benedictionem adjunctam habet. Sed missis querelis, Confessio ut ut non Scholastice, tamen admodum emphatice διχοτομίαν praedestinationis, in electionem, & reprobationem agnoscit, dum §. 2. praedestinatos in Christo vocat electos, extra Christum reprobos. Certe plus ex his intelligimus, quam si nomina, electionis, & reprobationis tantum, sine ullo elogio, creparet, praedicaret.
units.tr: VIII. Nor is the Confession an obstacle, which seems to take predestination only for election, excluding reprobation, since in §1 it says in explanation: God predestined, or chose, the saints from eternity. For the Confession, as it learned from Scripture the use of this word (as has just been said), so wished to keep it and speak with it. It adapted the common, well-known word, understood by all, to the particular species: what was indefinite and undetermined, it defined and determined. Moreover, the Confession does not press that Scholastic and Babylonian method, by which our age (alas!) grows blind, and which, being subtle rather than true, is rightly unsuited to the investigation of a matter of such importance; but it follows the method of the Holy Spirit speaking in Scripture, which alone the first restorers of the gospel religiously followed as useful. And since that method is the only true one, and is of God, and they who walked in it have, as the whole world witnesses, made more progress with us, for even the smallest thing which is from God and of God carries a blessing with it. But, leaving aside complaints, the Confession, although not in Scholastic fashion, nonetheless acknowledges quite emphatically the dichotomy of predestination into election and reprobation, when in §2 it calls the predestined in Christ elect, and those outside Christ reprobate. Certainly we understand more from these words than if it had merely named election and reprobation without any further qualification.

units.la: IX. Pergit autem Confessio in explicanda praedestinationis, seu electionis doctrina, ejusque §. 1. consideravit. 1. עושה[?] factorem, seu causam efficientem. 2. יסוד θεμέλιον fundamentum, quod est γῆν[?] ... εὐδοκία[?] 3. נצח aeternitatem.
units.tr: IX. The Confession goes on, in explaining the doctrine of predestination or election, and in §1 considers its: 1. factor [Hebrew: oseh], that is, the efficient cause. 2. foundation [Greek: themelion], which is [Greek words]. 3. eternity [Hebrew: netsach].

units.la: Quod ad primum attinet. Causa efficiens Praedestinationis vel electionis nostrae est Deus, h.e. Pater, Filius, & Sp. Sanctus. Patrem esse causam electionis probatur ex Eph. 1: 3 4. ς. Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ εὐλογήσας ἡμᾶς ἐν πάσῃ εὐλογίᾳ πνευματικῇ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ, καθὼς ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ. Benedictus Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui benedixit nobis omni benedictione spirituali, in coelestibus in Christo, quemadmodum elegit nos in ipso h.e. Deus Pater agnoscatur magnus, potens, gloriosus, peccatori bonus, & hic ἐπαινεθείη δόξα τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, laudetur gloria gratia ejus, celebretur, ametur, honoretur, qui prout me Paulum, & omnes fideles a mundo separavit, & quasi manu sua, ex pluribus assumsit; ita in tempore gratiosus, & liberalis, in me, & omnes fideles exstitit. Filium esse causam electionis, ipse Filius testatur. Ioh 15: 16. Οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἐξελέξασθε, ἀλλ' ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς. Non vos me elegistis; sed Ego elegi vos h.e. mea gratia, mea destinatione, & quod anima, charitas mea, & enixissima voluntas Patrem glorificandi, & fratres salvandi pro vobis ponit satisfactionem, a mundo separati estis, & v. 19. Ego elegi vos ex mundo, ideo odit vos mundus. Quod si quis scrupulose sibi imaginabitur, ut vulgo fieri solet, scripturam hic non agere de electione πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου; sed de electione, id est vocatione, quae fit tempore in sciat, utiamque hic inteltelligi; Vocatio enim in tempore sive ad vitam æternam, sive ad Apostolatum fit propter electionem æternam, illa est testis & signum hujus; sicut hæc est causa, & fundamentum illius. Nam Deo ab æterno cognita sunt omnia opera ejus, ita ut electio h. e. vocatio, quæ fit in tempore, certissimum sit argumentum electionis ante fundationem mundi. Sed & de Sp. Sancto, idem ex divinis ejus circa electos operibus colligitur. Eph. 1. 13. ἐν ᾧ καὶ πιστεύ-σαντες ἐσφραγίσθητε τῷ πνεύματι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῷ ἁγίῳ, 1. Cor. 6:11, ἀλλὰ ἡγιάσθητε, ἀλλὰ ἐδικαιώθητε, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν. Actor. 13. 2. εἶπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· ἀφορίσατέ δή μοι τὸν τε Βαρνάβαν καὶ τὸν Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον, ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς.
units.tr: As to the first point: the efficient cause of predestination or of our election is God, that is, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. That the Father is the cause of election is proved from Eph. 1:3-4: [Greek: Eulogētos ho Theos kai patēr tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou, ho eulogēsas hēmas en pasē eulogia pneumatikē en tois epouraniois en Christō, kathōs exelexato hēmas en autō]. Blessed be God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, as he chose us in him. That is, God the Father is to be acknowledged as great, powerful, glorious, and good to the sinner; and here [Greek: epainetheiē doxa tēs charitos autou], let the glory of his grace be praised, let him be celebrated, loved, and honoured, who, just as he separated me Paul and all the faithful from the world, and took us out from many as if with his own hand, so in time has shown himself gracious and generous towards me and all the faithful. That the Son is the cause of election the Son himself bears witness, John 15:16: [Greek: Ouch hymeis me exelexasthe, all' egō exelexamēn hymas]. You did not choose me, but I chose you; that is, by my grace, by my appointment, and because my soul, my love, and my most earnest will to glorify the Father and save the brethren, has put forward satisfaction on your behalf, you have been separated from the world. And v. 19: I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. But if anyone scrupulously imagines, as is commonly done, that Scripture here does not speak of election before the foundation of the world [pro katabolēs kosmou], but of election, that is, calling, which takes place in time, let him know that both are meant here. For calling in time, whether to eternal life or to apostleship, takes place on account of eternal election; the former is the witness and sign of the latter, just as the latter is the cause and foundation of the former. For all God's works were known to God from eternity, so that election, that is, calling which takes place in time, is a most certain proof of election before the foundation of the world. But the same is gathered concerning the Holy Spirit from his divine works toward the elect. Eph. 1:13: [Greek: en hō kai pisteusantes esphragisthēte tō pneumati tēs epangelias tō hagiō]; 1 Cor. 6:11: [Greek: alla hēgiasthēte, alla edikaiōthēte, en tō onomati tou kyriou Iēsou, kai en tō pneumati tou Theou hēmōn]; Acts 13:2: [Greek: eipen to pneuma to hagion: aphorisate dē moi ton te Barnaban kai ton Saulon eis to ergon, ho proskeklēmai autous].

units.la: X. Unde patet Deum causam esse, ut electionis, ita etiam reprobationis, qui enim ex omnibus aliquos tantum eligit, is alios non eligit, & proinde præterit in eligendo; adeoque reprobat. Hoc vult Scriptura, cum dicit אהבתי את יעקב ואת עשו שנאתי Mal. 1, 2. 3. ubi amor, significat gratiam & misericordiam erga Jacobum. Odium, judicium antece-dens mala opera ætatis & temporis consequentis Esavi, & in comparatione gratiæ, sive electionis Jacobi, ejus reprobationem. Unde ut Jacobus electorum: ita Esavus reproborum certum est exemplum. Chaldæus utitur voce רחיקית reprobavi, repuli, elongavi à me. Deinde Jer. 6: 30. כסף נמאס קראו להם כי מאס יהוה בהם argentum improbum vocati sunt, quia reprobavit Dominus ipsos. Syrus vertit [illegible, ~4 letters] argentum contemtum, despectum, reprobum, rejiciendum, abominandum.
units.tr: X. Hence it is plain that God is the cause of reprobation as well as of election. For whoever chooses some and not others from among all, does not choose the rest, and so passes them over in choosing, and thereby reprobates them. Scripture means this when it says, "I have loved Jacob, and hated Esau" (Mal. 1:2, 3) [אהבתי את יעקב ואת עשו שנאתי]. Here "love" signifies grace and mercy toward Jacob. "Hatred" signifies God's judgment, passed before the evil deeds of Esau in his later life and time, and, in comparison with the grace or election of Jacob, Esau's reprobation. Thus, as Jacob is a certain example of the elect, so Esau is a certain example of the reprobate. The Chaldee paraphrast uses the word רחיקית, I have rejected, I have pushed away, I have removed far from me. Again, Jer. 6:30: "They shall be called reprobate silver, because the Lord has reprobated them" [כסף נמאס קראו להם כי מאס יהוה בהם]. The Syriac renders this by a word of about four letters, meaning despised, rejected, reprobate, to be cast away, abominable.

units.la: XI. Quod ad secundum, seu fundamentum electionis attinet; illud est merum Dei beneplacitum, quo in certis quibusdam hominibus gratiosam suam gratiam manifestare voluit. 2. Timoth. 1:9. 10. Τῷ σώσαντι ἡμᾶς, καὶ καλέσαντι κλήσει ἁγίᾳ, οὐ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ κατ' ἰδίαν πρόθεσιν, καὶ χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων, φανερωθεῖσαν δὲ νῦν διὰ τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ [?]. [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters] * [illegible, ~30 letters] Ille qui servavit nos & vocavit nos vocatione sanctâ;non secundum (sicut) opera nostra. sed secundum voluntatem suam,& bonitatem suam:illam (scil.) quæ data est nobis in Jesu Christo ante tempus æternitatum. Et revelata est jam in revelatione servatoris nostri Jesu Christi. [illegible, ~30 letters]
units.tr: XI. As for the second point, that is, the foundation of election: it is the pure good pleasure of God, by which he willed to make his gracious grace manifest in certain men. 2 Tim. 1:9, 10: "Who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and the grace given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times, but now made manifest through the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ" [Τῷ σώσαντι ἡμᾶς, καὶ καλέσαντι κλήσει ἁγίᾳ, οὐ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ κατ' ἰδίαν πρόθεσιν, καὶ χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων, φανερωθεῖσαν δὲ νῦν διὰ τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ]. He who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own will and his own goodness, namely that which was given to us in Jesus Christ before the time of the ages. And it is now revealed in the revelation of our Saviour Jesus Christ. [illegible in scan]

units.la: [illegible, ~40 letters] Qui servat & vocat nos vocatione sanctâ, non sicut conveniebat ([illegible, ~6 letters] par erat, conveniebat, consentiebat, concordabat) operibus nostris, sed prout [illegible, ~4 letters] proprium (& peculiare) erat propositi ipsius, & gratia ipsius, quam dedit nobis (quâ nos donati sumus) in Iesu Christo ante annos aeternos. Magnum est hoc & confessum, jámque apparet modò per apparitionem Iesu Christi Servatoris nostri. Ubi nota, exquisitum & de industria selectum esse ab Apostolo vocabulum προθέσεως, secundùm quod factam Praedestinationem nostram ubique praedicat, quod est כלין חרין consummatio decisa נחרצה finale decisum יצר סמוך propositum nixum, cogitatio fulta, firma, certa, decretum fixum, adeóque non pendens aliunde; sed in Dei beneplacito radicatum, cujus ipsum poenitere non potest, quod effectum jam dedit, & porrò dabit, quod propositum, seu decretum beneplaciti, est gratia, favor, benevolentia, misericordia, amor, quô, tanquam sorte notati, & definiti sumus. Est igitur electio nostra secundùm propositum, seu beneplacitum, & quidem efficax h. e. quod certò assequitur finem, non quod bonum aliquod in nobis invenerit h. e. quòd, vel vocantem in tempore Deum non frustremur, vel vocationi ex nobis obsequamur, & opportunitate intrandi in regnum Dei utamur; sed quòd Deus id operatur, quod proposuit; quia nempe in proposito est voluntas, & in voluntate consilium sapiens, quô judicavit ad manifestationem, & laudem gloriae suae facere, ut ita faciat, h. e. ut atratos sublimet salute.
units.tr: He who saves and calls us with a holy calling, not as our works deserved (what was fitting, equal, agreeable, in accord), but according to what was proper and peculiar to his own purpose, and his own grace, which he gave us (by which we were granted) in Jesus Christ before the eternal ages. This is great and acknowledged, and it now appears through the appearing of Jesus Christ our Saviour. Here note that the word προθέσεως was chosen with care and deliberately by the Apostle, since it everywhere proclaims our predestination as something made. It corresponds to the Hebrew terms כלין חרין (a decided consummation), נחרצה (a decided end), and יצר סמוך (a purpose resting upon something): a settled purpose, a firm, fixed, certain thought, a fixed decree, and therefore not dependent on anything else, but rooted in the good pleasure of God, which cannot repent of itself, which has already produced its effect and will produce it further. This purpose, or decree of good pleasure, is grace, favour, benevolence, mercy and love, by which we have been, as it were, marked with a lot and defined. Our election is therefore according to purpose, or good pleasure, and indeed it is effective, that is, it certainly attains its end. It does not find in us some good, whether that we do not frustrate God calling in time, or that we obey the calling from ourselves and make use of the opportunity to enter the kingdom of God. Rather, God works out what he has purposed, because in the purpose there is will, and in the will a wise counsel, by which he judged to make it for the manifestation and praise of his glory, that is, to exalt the clothed ones to salvation.

units.la: XII. Sicut autem electionis fundamentum est mera Dei gratia, & beneplacitum: ita etiam reprobationis causa nulla est praeter divinum beneplacitum. Cujus vult miseretur, quem vult indurat h. e. Deus pro suo beneplacito, non tantùm miseratur; sed etiam indurat & judicat. ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τῆς πηλοῦ, ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι, ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος, ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν; Aut non habet potestatem figulus luti ex eadem massa ut faciat aliud quidem ad honorem vas, aliud verò ad ignominiam. [illegible, ~30 letters]
units.tr: XII. But just as the foundation of election is the mere grace and good pleasure of God, so also the cause of reprobation is nothing other than the divine good pleasure. "He has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills," that is, God, according to his good pleasure, not only shows mercy but also hardens and judges. "Or has not the potter power over the clay, to make out of the same lump one vessel to honour and another to dishonour?" [ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τῆς πηλοῦ, ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι, ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος, ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;] "Or does not the potter of clay have power to make from the same lump one vessel indeed for honour, and another for dishonour?" units.la: *الفاخراني ليس له سلطان على الطين ان يعمل من [?] الفخار نفسها إنا للكرامة وإنا للاهانة [?] Aut an figulo non est potestas (dominium) in lutum, ut facere ex massa eadem vas ad honorem & vas ad turpitudinem. Quam parabolam figuli & φυράματος [?] massae sive πηλὸς [?] luti refero. Primò ad beneplacitum, & potestatem eligendi, adeoque miserendi, & reprobandi in specie; ut enim figulus potest facere ut ipsi placet vas aliud ad honorem ex eodem luto, unde est vas ad dedecus, quod in vilitate luti relinquitur: ita etiam Deus potest misereri, quorum vult ex peccatoribus, & reprobare adeoque negligere quos vult: quia non fit injuria peccatori, si reprobetur, adeoque negligatur, etiam si Deus alterius peccatoris misereatur, quem admodum non fit injuria matulae, si in vilitate luti relinquatur: Secundo ad libertatem consilii Dei de homine. Nam cùm Deus viderit, se hominem in mutabili rectitudine posse condere, & sic regere juste & pulchrè, ut regiminis exitus sit demonstratio gloriae gratiae in quibusdam, justitiae in aliis: quid ipsum potuit impedire? aut quae erat ejus, qui nondum erat, dignitas, ut aliter de eo statueretur? Potuit id Deus liberè & juste velle; Si enim non injustum est hominem jam creatum sic regere, ut eveniat, ut in eo potentia & gratia Dei demonstretur; non etiam injustum est id ab æterno velle; namDeus ut vidit se juste, & rectè facere posse, ita voluit, neque quemquam sine consilio creavit aut produxit. Neque tamen creatio est medium damnationis, quia ex ea glorificatur Deus ut bonus; sed tota gubernatio est medium demonstrandi variam gloriam Dei: damnationis autem causa peccatum est; sed praeteritionis beneplacitum: quem vult, indurat.
units.tr: The Arabic here renders Romans 9:21 as: "Has not the potter authority over the clay, to make from the same clay one vessel for honour and another for dishonour?" [transliterated: al-fakhkhar... laysa lahu sultan 'ala al-tin an ya'mal min...] Or has not the potter power (dominion) over the clay, to make out of the same lump a vessel for honour and a vessel for shame. I refer this parable of the potter and of the lump (φυράματος) or clay (πηλὸς) first to the good pleasure and power of election, and so to the power of showing mercy and of reprobating in particular cases. For just as the potter can make, as he pleases, one vessel for honour from the same clay, and from the remainder of the clay there is a vessel for dishonour, which is left in the baseness of the clay, so God can show mercy to whom he wills among sinners, and reprobate, and so pass over those whom he wills. For no injury is done to a sinner if he is reprobated and so passed over, just as no injury is done to a pot if it is left in the baseness of the clay, even if God shows mercy to another sinner. Second, I refer it to the freedom of God's counsel concerning man. For since God foresaw that he could found man in changeable uprightness, and so govern him justly and beautifully, that the outcome of the government would be a demonstration of the glory of grace in some and of justice in others, what could have hindered him? Or what dignity had he who did not yet exist, that he should be determined otherwise? God could will this freely and justly. For if it is not unjust to govern man already created in such a way that the power and grace of God are shown in him, neither is it unjust to will this from eternity. For God, as he saw that he could act justly and rightly, so willed, and he created or produced no one without counsel. Yet creation is not the means of damnation, since God is glorified in it as good. Rather, the whole governance is the means of displaying the varied glory of God. The cause of damnation, however, is sin; but the good pleasure of passing over is the cause of the rest: "whom he wills, he hardens."

units.la: XIII. Quo verò sensu dicatur Deus indurare consultum duximus breviter expedire. Nempe induratio consideratur à Paulo, ut actio Dei, & significat 1. judicium illud Dei, quo homo dignus est, qui exsors maneat gratiae ejus, & hoc judicium Deus necessariò de omni carne facit: omnes enim sumus indigni, ἢ πᾶς ὁ κόσμος ὑπόδικος ἐσι τῷ Θεῷ. Quamvis igitur sine hoc judicio non sit induratio, ipsum tamen non est induratio, nam quorundam eorum, quos judicat exsortes gratiae, miserertur. 2. voluntatem judicium hoc exsequendi. 3. non impertitionem Spiritus sui & timoris. 4. permissionem tentationis diabolicae. 5. beneficia temporalia, & nominatim dationem animi magni, & imperterriti, quo homo abusurus est ad opponendum se Deo. Haec à parte Dei. Sed homo indurat seipsum, quando, audito verbo adjurationis benedictionem, & maledictionem proponentis, sibi benedicit, & non timet, beneficiisque ac longanimitate Dei abutitur.
units.tr: XIII. In what sense it is said that God hardens, we have thought it useful to explain briefly. Namely, hardening is considered by Paul as an action of God, and it signifies first that judgment of God by which a man is worthy to remain without his grace. God necessarily passes this judgment upon all flesh, for we are all unworthy, since "all the world is liable to God" [ἡ πᾶς ὁ κόσμος ὑπόδικος ἐστι τῷ Θεῷ]. Although, therefore, without this judgment there is no hardening, the judgment itself is not hardening, for he has mercy on some of those whom he judges to be without grace. Second, the will to carry out this judgment. Third, the non-imparting of his Spirit and of the fear of God. Fourth, the permission of diabolical temptation. Fifth, temporal benefits, and especially the giving of a great and fearless spirit, which a man will abuse to set himself against God. These are on God's side. But man hardens himself when, having heard the word of adjuration which sets forth blessing and cursing, he blesses himself and does not fear, and abuses the benefits and long-suffering of God.

units.la: XIV. Qua verò electio & reprobatio pendet à beneplacito, & libertate eâ consilii Dei, quam habet figulus in lutum, sequitur I. Deum nullo modo, alios eligendo, alios reprobando esse personarum acceptorem, quia non judicat nisi secundum legem suam, quæ est speculum veritatis justitiæ & judicii Dei: homo peccat adeoque in acceptionem personarum incidit, quia non voluntatem suam; sed Dei pro regula, & norma actionum suarum habet, quam si transgrediatur reus est. Deus peccare, adeoque personam accipere, non potest; quia voluntatem suam pro regula & norma actionum suarum habet, atque ita facit quod ipsi lubet. Neque Deus recognoscit quenquam dignum gratia sua sanctificante, & justificante, nihilque in homine peccatore tanti facit, ut sit ipsi causa gratiam suam donandi, sive sit generis nobilitas, ut quòd Judæi carnis privilegio superbientes filii Abrahami audiebant, sive divitiæ, sive sapientia: qualis erat in Græcis; hæc enim omnia apud Deum sunt זבל[?] stercora, & abominatio mera. Accedit, quòd προσωπολήψια[?] faciei acceptio, contingit in distributione bonorum debitorum, cum unus alteri, sine justa ratione præfertur, quæ Deo gratiam suam ex mero beneplacito dispensante, ut indigna est: ita in eum cadere non potest; sed libera donorum, ut corporalium, & terrestrium: ita spiritualium, & cœlestium distributio, Deo non est indigna, adeoque ut absolutus, summus, & independens, omnium rerum dominus, eam sibi vendicat. II. Deum causam reprobationis, non esse auctorem peccati, cum reprobatio ejus causa non sit; electi enim reprobati non sunt, tamen peccant, & quamvis peccati permissionem decreverit, ut justitiam suam in ejus gloriosa condemnatione ostendat, nullo tamen jure, peccati existentia, ei ut causæ adscribi potest: differunt enim peccatum, & permissio ejus, ut actio illa hominis in qua est legis divinæ transgressio, & gubernatio demonstrandi exinde justitiam Dei. Et quanquam peccatum, atque hominis damnatio ad reprobationem consequantur, illa tamen nonnisi interveniente libero hominis arbitrio, & voluntate summâ cum delectatione peccante, consequuntur, quod unum, ut ad omnem peccatori excusationem demendam sufficit: ita extante peccato, Deum nullam cum peccatore communionem, & similitudinis testificationem habentem, adjustum, & necessarium judicium provocat. III. Hominem omnem non aliter esse in manu Dei, quàm lutum in manu figuli, posse igitur Deum, prout ipsi lubet, de homine statuere, & disponere. Hominem nihil habere, propter quod à Deo ametur, quia lutum nihil habet antequam à figulo præparetur. Discant ergo Reges, Barones, Nobiles se esse lutum, nihil se amplius habere, quàm habent abjecta mundi, nullam præ illis naturæ præstantiam; sed eandem luti vilitatem. Discant Reges, Barones, Nobiles tunc se debere erubescere, vultum suum fatigari, dolore, & pudore affici, si se, qualesnam naturâ suâ sint, intelligerent, quando homines ejusdem naturæ sibi supplices fiunt. Discant R. B. N. Deo gratias agere, cùm illos æque poterat in sua vilitate relinquere, sed & discant fe humiliare, & cum tremore Filium Regis exosculari. Sciant Reges terræ, Altissimum habere in regno hominum potestatem, & eum posse Reges, ut transferre; ita erigere. Sciant Reges terræ, Regis Filium esse Regem, & cum validis terræ regibus magnos populos habentibus spolium dividere, non minorem, quàm Reges maximos possidere hæreditatem, & ipsis insciis, invitis, imò ipsi mentientibus, in medio regni eorum, & posse, & velle regnum suum erigere. Discant & Docti, accensæ, in domo Dei, lucernæ, fe esse testam & lutum, discant fe ornatos esse luce Scripturæ, tanquam aliquo gypso, à Magno illo Figulo; discant donum prophetiæ esse in testaceis vasculis, ut ejus præstantia, & supereminentia fit solus ipse Deus; discant fe non eò usque in doctrina profecifle, ut majori profectu non indigeant, neque fe esse vasa, ita à Magno isto figulo ornata, ut majorem adhuc non possint recipere ornatum; discant suâ non superbire doctrinâ, & suum tamdiu splendere gypsum, quamdiu ex Sole justitiæ radii incidant in ipsum; discant denique, intendántque, radios ex illo Sole incidentes & in fe receptos, in alios etiam minus fplendicantes reflectere. IV. Electos à primo ipso momento, quo electionis suæ certitudine donantur, per totam vitam debere Deo, pro tanto amoris gratuiti privilegio, gratias agere. Magnum est privilegium amari à Rege, certè majus à Deo: magnum est privilegium eligi in consiliarium Regis, certè majus est, admyfteria piecatis, in quæ ipsi quoq; Angeli cupiunt introspicere, intelligenda affumi, profunda divinæ sapientiæ arcana haftenus mundo incognita, Christo æterno Dei filio, fidelissimo nostro Præceptore interprete intelligere, atque ita consiliorum divinorum participes fieri. Magna dignitas est Regis filium esse; sed certè major Dei; qui enim filius Dei est, non vanæ & præter labentis; sed æternæ gloriæ hæres est. O beatos, & gloriosos quibus S. sanctus digitus ille Dei, in tabulis cordis hæc scribit! Non elt hoccum omni mundi gloria commutandum. Seftentur alii Regias Regis Affveri epulas, gaudeant ad citharas, & nablia; verùm æterna, pro electione nostra, gratiarum actio noftrum fit epulum, & perpetuum, quòd nomina nostra scripta sint in cœlis, gaudium!
units.tr: XIV. Since election and reprobation depend on God's good pleasure and on that freedom of counsel which the potter has over the clay, it follows, first, that God is in no way a respecter of persons when He elects some and reprobates others, because He judges only according to His law, which is the mirror of the truth of justice and of God's judgment. A man who sins falls into respect of persons, because he does not take God's will as the rule and norm of his actions, and if he transgresses it he is guilty. God cannot sin, and so cannot respect persons, because He has His own will as the rule and norm of His actions, and thus does what pleases Him. Nor does God recognise anyone as worthy of His sanctifying and justifying grace, and He sets no such value on anything in a sinful man that it could move Him to bestow His grace, whether it be nobility of birth, as the Jews proudly boasted in the privilege of the flesh, sons of Abraham, or riches, or wisdom, as among the Greeks. For all these things are with God dung [זבל], and sheer abomination. Moreover, respect of persons [προσωπολημψία] occurs in the distribution of things owed, when one person is preferred to another without just reason. But God's grace is given from His pure and bountiful good pleasure, and so it is not owed; therefore respect of persons cannot fall upon Him in this matter. The free distribution of gifts, of bodily and earthly goods, and likewise of spiritual and heavenly ones, is not unworthy of God, and so He, as absolute, supreme and independent Lord of all things, claims this right for Himself. II. Second, God is not the author of sin, since His reprobation is not its cause. For the reprobate do not sin because they are reprobated, and the elect are not without sin. Although He has decreed to permit sin, in order to show His justice in the glorious condemnation of the wicked, yet the existence of sin cannot rightly be ascribed to Him as its cause. For sin and its permission differ: sin is that action of man in which the divine law is transgressed, while permission is the governance by which the justice of God is thence displayed. And although sin and the damnation of man follow upon reprobation, they follow only through the intervening free choice and will of man, who sins with the greatest delight. This one fact is enough to remove every excuse from the sinner. So, while sin remains, God, who has no fellowship with the sinner and no witness of likeness to him, calls forth a just and necessary judgment. III. Every man is in the hand of God no otherwise than the clay is in the hand of the potter; God can therefore determine and dispose of man as He pleases. Man has nothing on account of which he is loved by God, for the clay has nothing before it is shaped by the potter. Let kings, barons and nobles learn, then, that they are clay, that they have nothing more than the cast-off things of the world, no natural excellence above others, but the same worthlessness of clay. Let kings, barons and nobles learn that they ought then to blush, that their faces should be made to grow pale and be overcome with grief and shame, if they understood what they are by nature, when men of the same nature become suppliants to them. Let the barons and nobles learn to give thanks to God, since He could equally have left them in their worthlessness; but let them also learn to humble themselves and with trembling to kiss the Son of the King. Let the kings of the earth know that the Most High has power over the kingdoms of men, and that He can raise up kings as easily as He can remove them. Let the kings of the earth know that the Son of the King is King, and that, dividing the spoil with the mighty kings of the earth who have great peoples, He possesses an inheritance no less than the greatest kings, and that, even against their knowledge and their will, indeed while they lie, He both can and wills to raise up His kingdom in the midst of their kingdoms. Let the learned also learn, that they are lamps lit in the house of God, that they are earthenware and clay; let them learn that they are adorned with the light of Scripture, as with some plaster, by that great Potter; let them learn that the gift of prophecy is held in earthen vessels, so that its excellence and supereminence may be God alone; let them learn that they have not advanced so far in doctrine that they have no need of greater progress, nor that they are vessels so adorned by that great Potter that they cannot receive a still greater adornment; let them not pride themselves on their learning, and let their plaster shine only as long as the rays of the Sun of righteousness fall upon it; let them finally take care to reflect the rays that fall upon them from that Sun and are received within them, also to others who shine less brightly. IV. The elect, from the very first moment in which they are granted the certainty of their election, ought to give thanks to God throughout their whole life for so great a privilege of free love. It is a great privilege to be loved by a king, and certainly a greater one to be loved by God. It is a great privilege to be chosen as the king's counsellor, and certainly greater to be taken up into understanding of the mysteries of godliness, into which even the angels desire to look; to understand the deep secrets of divine wisdom, hitherto unknown to the world, with Christ, the eternal Son of God, our most faithful Teacher and Interpreter, and so to become partakers of the divine counsels. It is a great dignity to be the son of a king, but certainly a greater one to be the son of God; for he who is the son of God is heir not of vain and passing glory, but of eternal glory. O blessed and glorious are they, on whose hearts that holy finger of God writes these things on the tablets of the heart! This is not to be exchanged for all the glory of the world. Let others boast of the royal feasts of King Ahasuerus, let them rejoice at the harp and the psaltery; but for our election, the thanksgiving of eternal praise shall be our feast, and our perpetual joy, that our names are written in heaven!

units.la: XV. Quia vero Deus sanctos ab æterno prædestinavit vel elegit liberè, & merâ suâ gratiâ, rectè infert Confessio. Nullo ergo hominum respectu, h.e. non ex fide prævisa, neque propter bona opera, & si quid aliud (à mente hic sanè fibulandâ) excogitari potest. Et certè ii qui volunt electionem ex fide & operibus suspendere, quamvis jactent gratiam, eam tamen nullo modo agnoscere possunt. Εἰ γὰρ ἐκ χάριτος, οὐκ ἔτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις. Εἰ δὲ ἐξ ἔργων, οὐκ ἔτι ἐστὶ χάρις, ἐπεὶ τὸ ἔργον οὐκ ἔτι ἐστὶν ἔ-ργον, h.e. gratia non relinquit locum operi nec fidei, nec opus, nec fides prævisa relinquunt locum gratiæ; quia gratia, significat voluntatem salvandi, indignum & non merentem, fides autem, & opera praevisa, dignum & merentem, qui igitur dicunt nos electos esse ex fide praevisa, & propter bona opera, dicunt electionem, seu voluntatem salvandi non esse ex gratia. Ita Syrus. [illegible, ~40 letters] [illegible, ~40 letters] Si vero per gratiam (reliquiae manserunt) non est ex operibus, & si non, gratia non esset gratia: si vero per opera, non est ex gratia; & si non, opus non esset opus. Sic Arabs. [illegible, ~35 letters] [illegible, ~35 letters] Quod si per gratiam existant (reliquiae,) utique non est ex operibus quoquomodo; & si non, certè gratia non existeret gratia quoquomodo. Quòd si sit ex operibus, utique non est hæc gratia ullatenus: & si non, certè opus non esset opus ullatenus. Demonstrat hoc Confessio ex Epistola sancti Pauli 2. Timoth. 1.9.10. (quem locum vide § XI.) Qui salvos fecit nos, & vocavit vocatione sanctâ non secundum opera nostra; sed secundum suum propositum, & gratiam quae data est nobis, &c. h.e. Nos neque ad salutem procurandam, vel ad vocationem nostri sanctam quicquam contulimus, neque quicquam in nobis, vel fuisse, vel a Deo praevisum esse, quare nos in tempore vocaret, ergo multo minus fuisse, ex quo, & propter quod eligeret.
units.tr: XV. Because God elected or predestined the saints from eternity freely and by His mere grace, the Confession rightly infers: with no regard to men, that is, not from faith foreseen, nor on account of good works, nor on account of anything else that might be thought of (which must be carefully kept in mind here). And certainly those who wish to make election depend on faith and works, although they boast of grace, can in no way acknowledge it. For if it is of grace, it is no longer of works, since grace would no longer be grace; but if it is of works, it is no longer grace, since the work would no longer be work [Εἰ γὰρ ἐκ χάριτος, οὐκ ἔτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις. Εἰ δὲ ἐξ ἔργων, οὐκ ἔτι ἐστὶ χάρις, ἐπεὶ τὸ ἔργον οὐκ ἔτι ἐστὶν ἔργον]. That is, grace leaves no room for works nor for faith; nor do works or faith foreseen leave any room for grace; for grace signifies the will to save the unworthy and undeserving, whereas faith and foreseen works signify the worthy and deserving. Therefore those who say that we are elected from foreseen faith and on account of good works say that election, or the will to save, is not from grace. So the Syriac: [illegible passage of about forty letters] [illegible passage of about forty letters]. But if by grace (the remainder survives) it is not of works, and if not, grace would not be grace: but if by works, it is not of grace; and if not, the work would not be work. So the Arabic: [illegible passage of about thirty-five letters] [illegible passage of about thirty-five letters]. But if they exist by grace (the remainder), then certainly it is not of works in any way; and if not, certainly grace would not exist as grace in any way. But if it is of works, then certainly this is not grace in any way; and if not, certainly the work would not be work in any way. The Confession proves this from the Epistle of St Paul to Timothy, 2 Tim. 1.9, 10 (see the passage at § XI): who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and the grace which was given us, etc. That is, we contributed nothing either to the procuring of our salvation or to our holy calling, nor was there anything in us, or foreseen by God in us, on account of which He would call us in time; much less therefore was there anything from which, or on account of which, He would elect us.

units.la: XVI. Quemadmodum autem Deus ab aeterno elegit homines, non ex fide praevisâ, neque propter bona opera; sed ex mera sua gratia: ita etiam reprobavit, h.e. neglexit, non propter mala opera, neque propter incredulitatem, h.e. quòd fidem non sint habituri; sed ex mero beneplacito h.e. q. ipsi ita placuit. Venis divitem, & praegnantem sanè habemus locum Sancti Pauli ad Rom. 9.21. Aut non habet potestatem figulus &c. Vides! jus, potestas, beneplacitum Dei in hominem, par est ei juri, potestati, & beneplacito, quod figulus habet in lutum, uti enim figulus potestatem habet ex eadem conspersione facere vas in honorem aliud, aliud in usum in honorum: ita etiam Deus habet potestatem miserendi, cujus vult miserescere, & indurandi quem vult, ita ut ille sit vas misericordiae ad gloriam, alter fiat vas irae ad interitum, licet ejusdem conspersionis illi sint, non tantum τῆς αὐτῆς Φύσεως unius & ejusdem naturae; sed etiam τῶν αὐτῶν προαιρέσεων, earundem voluntatum h.e. homines dum in mente Dei considerarentur, nullam fidem, nullam incredulitatem, nulla opera, sive bona ea sint, sive mala, habuerunt. Quia Praedestinatio, adeóque electio, & reprobatio, (ut sobrius, pius, & modestus Theologus Amesius, ut in hac Praedestinationis doctrina; ita in omnibus aliis Confessioni Helveticae addictissimus, pie, & satis profunde ait) nec terminum, nec objectum suum, adeóque conditionem objecti, necessario praesupponit ut existens; sed ponit ut existat: ita ut vi praedestinationis ordinetur ut sit; quia praedestinatio est voluntas Dei, quae non praesupponit objectum; sed volendo ponit & facit, h.e. nulla in praedestinatione aeterna fuit inter praedestinatos differentia quam differentiam Deus praedestinans necessario sequutus fuisset; sed si quae apparet, ea ex decreto praedestinationis consequuta est. Quod ipsum Sanctus Paulus in Jacobo, & Esavo, tanquam electorum & reproborum typo demonstrat, v. 11-12. 13. μὴ πω γὰρ γεννηθέντων, μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ κακόν, ἵνα ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόθεσις μένῃ, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ, ὅτι ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι· καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.
units.tr: XVI. Just as God chose men from eternity, not on the basis of foreseen faith or because of good works, but from his mere grace, so too he reprobated them, that is, passed them over, not because of evil works or because of unbelief, that is, because they would not have faith, but from his mere good pleasure, that is, because it so pleased him. Here we have a rich and very pointed passage, Rom. 9:21: Hath not the potter power over the clay, &c.? You see that the right, power, and good pleasure of God over man is like the right, power, and good pleasure that a potter has over the clay. For just as the potter, from the same lump, has the power to make one vessel for honour and another for common use, so God has the power to show mercy on whom he wills and to harden whom he wills, so that one becomes a vessel of mercy unto glory and the other becomes a vessel of wrath unto destruction. They are of the same lump, not only of the same nature [τῆς αὐτῆς Φύσεως] of one and the same kind, but also of the same purposes [τῶν αὐτῶν προαιρέσεων], of the same wills; that is, when men were considered in the mind of God, they had no faith, no unbelief, and no works, whether good or evil. For predestination, and therefore election and reprobation (as the sober, pious, and modest theologian Amesius, who was most devoted to the Helvetic Confession in this doctrine of predestination as in all others, rightly and quite profoundly says), does not presuppose its term and object as existing, and so not the condition of the object, but posits that they should exist. So by the force of predestination it is ordained that they should be; for predestination is the will of God, which does not presuppose its object but, by willing, posits and makes it. That is, in eternal predestination there was no difference among the predestined which God, predestining, would necessarily have followed; but if any difference appears, it has followed from the decree of predestination. The apostle Paul himself demonstrates this in Jacob and Esau as types of the elect and the reprobate, vv. 11–13: "For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth, it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated" [μὴ πω γὰρ γεννηθέντων, μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ κακόν, ἵνα ἡ κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόθεσις μένῃ, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ, ὅτι ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι· καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα].

units.la: Dum nondum nati sunt filii ejus; neque fecerunt bonum aut malum, prius cognita est electio Dei, ut illa permaneret: non per opera, sed per manum ejus, qui vocavit: Dictum enim est, quòd senior futurus sit servus minori: Sicuti dictum est, Jacobum dilexi, & Hisavum odi.
units.tr: While her sons were not yet born and had done neither good nor evil, the election of God was declared beforehand, so that it might stand, not by works but by him who calls: for it was said to her that the elder would serve the younger, as it is written, "Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated."

units.la: Et non erant filii ejus jam nati, neque fecerant quicquam bonum aut malum; ut permaneret propositum Dei, quod peculiare est (proprie convenit) ejus arbitrio. Non ex operibus sed ex vocante: Dictum illi est, quòd major famulaturus sit minori: Sicuti scriptum est, utique ego dilexi Jacobum, & aversatus sum Hisavum. Ubi observo I. Distinctionem inter Jacobum, & Esavum, Jacobo imperium cum regno, Esavo servitus delegata fuit. Quorum illud praerogativam vocationis, & depositi oraculorum Dei, ac Testamentorum, & sanctuarii, & feminis electi, & Christi ex ipso (procedet stella ex Jacobo, & exurget sceptrum ex Israële) & ad ipsum, cum regno venturi, includebat. Hæc conditionem deteriorem, separationem ab hæreditate, (servi enim est, non manere in domo) & involuntariam suis temporibus famulationem, qualis est hypocritarum, reproborum, & Christo mentientium, importat. II. Causam distinctionis inter Jacobum, & Esavum, quæ non sunt opera, quæ fecerint vel Esau, vel Jacob; quia hoc oraculum editum est, antequam pueri quicquam boni, vel mali fecissent, quod argumentum inde vim habet; quia oraculum hoc secundum partem duriorem, est pronunciatio sententiæ, & judicium. Si odium & reprobatio Esavi a sequentibus demum factis ejus penderet, non fuisset sententia pronunciata, antequam ea fecisset. III. Amorem Dei fecisse discrimen & distinctionem inter Jacobum, & Esavum, non meritum illius, neque demeritum hujus. Q. Esavus Jacobo frater fuit, h. e. Quia Deus nihil vidit in alterutro, quare huic magis, quam illi benefaceret; sed tantum hoc, quod fratres essent. IV. Jacobo non suffragata fuisse opera sua, ut amaretur; sed ex Dei amore fuisse fidem, & opera consequentia, quibus ejus fides fuit demonstrata, qui amor est προθεσις κατ' ἐκλογὴν[?] h. e. propositum in quo est הַבְדָּלָה[?] separatio, seu electio, cui opposita est ἀπώθησις[?] rejectio seu odium, h. e. rejectio a spirituali bono, cui proposito attribuitur effectus κλήσις vocatio h. e. adductio per gratiam potentem, & Spiritum. V. Alioqui potuisse Deum, æque Jacobum præterire, atque Esavum. VI. Neque Esavo obfuisse, quo minus potenter vocaretur, vel opera, vel quicquam aliud. VII. Eandem fuisse Jacobi, & Esavi, in prædestinationis decreto æterno ad gratiam propinquitatem, & eandem gratiæ indignitatem, hoc est, quemadmodum electus est Jacob, ita poterat eligi Esau, & quemadmodum reprobatus est Esau, ita poterat reprobari Jacob. Quam indignitatis & propinquitatis utriusque ad gratiam in æterno prædestinationis decreto considerationem, voluit Deus nobis certis signis declarare, 1. quod uterque, ex Isac, & Rebecca essent, 2. quod eadem conceptione, adeoque fratres essent.
