units.tr: And his sons had not yet been born, nor had they done anything good or bad, so that the purpose of God, which is peculiar to (properly belongs to) his will, might remain: not from works but from him who calls. It was said to her that the greater would serve the lesser, as it is written: "Indeed I have loved Jacob, and I have turned away from Esau." Here I note the following. I. A distinction between Jacob and Esau: to Jacob was given rule together with the kingdom, to Esau servitude. The former included the privilege of the calling, the trust of the oracles of God, of the covenants, of the sanctuary, of the chosen seed, and of Christ, who from him (a star shall come forth from Jacob, and a sceptre shall rise from Israel) and to him would come with the kingdom. The latter brings a worse condition, separation from the inheritance (for a servant does not remain in the house), and a servitude in its own time that is involuntary, such as belongs to hypocrites, reprobates, and those who lie to Christ. II. The cause of the distinction between Jacob and Esau is not works, which either Esau or Jacob had done; because this oracle was uttered before the boys had done anything good or evil, and this argument has force from that fact; because this oracle, in its harsher part, is a pronouncement of sentence and a judgment. If the hatred and rejection of Esau had depended on his later deeds, the sentence would not have been pronounced before he had done them. III. The love of God made the difference and distinction between Jacob and Esau, not the merit of the one or the demerit of the other. Q. Esau was a brother to Jacob, that is, because God saw nothing in either of them, why he should do good to this one rather than that one; but only this, that they were brothers. IV. Jacob's works did not help him to be loved; rather, from God's love came his faith, and the works that follow, by which his faith was shown. This love is purpose [πρόθεσις κατ' ἐκλογήν], in which there is separation [הַבְדָּלָה], or election, opposed to which is rejection [ἀπώθησις], or hatred, that is, rejection from the spiritual good; to this purpose is attributed the effect of calling [κλήσις], that is, leading by powerful grace and the Spirit. V. Otherwise God could have passed over Jacob just as well as Esau. VI. Nor did anything hinder Esau from being powerfully called, whether works or anything else. VII. In the eternal decree of predestination there was the same nearness of Jacob and Esau to grace, and the same unworthiness for grace; that is, just as Jacob was elected, so Esau could have been elected, and just as Esau was reprobated, so Jacob could have been reprobated. God wished to declare to us, by certain signs, this consideration in the eternal decree of predestination of the unworthiness and nearness of each to grace: 1. that both were from Isaac and Rebecca; 2. that they were conceived at the same time, and so were brothers.

units.la: XVII. Ex hoc electionis, & reprobationis æternæ exemplo discimus, cur David suam adeoque & nostram prædestinationem seu electionem, dicat tremendam separationem Psal. 139. 14. Quia scilicet primo tremenda est separatio, quæ fit cum demonstratione simul iræ, & gratiæ, bonitatis & severitatis, bonitatis & gratiæ, in Jacobo: Iræ & severitatis in Esavo. Secundo quia profundissimum & inexplicabile continet mysterium consilii, & providentiæ divinæ, quâ permisit hominem labi, & humanum genus reum fieri, ordinavit sponsorem, & ex nihilo deterioribus quosdam rejecit, ut Esavum, quosdam assumfit, ut Jacobum. Amplius quia in hac separatione Deus se admirabilem ostendit, & eos, quos separa-vit, vit,[?] admirabiles, & tanquam signa, & prodigia facit. Jef.8.18. הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי יהוה לאתות ולמופתים בישראל Ecce ego, & pueri, quos dedit mihi Dominus, in signa, & prodigia sumus in Israele. Christus mediator, & discipuli ejus electi, fuerunt portenta in Israële, propter facta qualia nunquam videbant; & propter dicta, siquidem homo nunquam ita ut ipse, h.e. ad conscientiam, loquutus fuerit.
units.tr: XVII. From this example of eternal election and reprobation we learn why David calls his predestination, and so ours, or election, a fearful separation (Ps. 139:14). For, first, the separation is fearful, since it happens with a demonstration at once of wrath and of grace, of goodness and of severity, of goodness and of grace in Jacob, and of wrath and severity in Esau. Second, because it contains the most profound and inexplicable mystery of the divine counsel and providence, by which he permitted man to fall and the human race to become guilty, appointed a surety, and from nothing rejected some as worse, like Esau, and took others, like Jacob. Further, because in this separation God shows himself wonderful, and makes those whom he has separated wonderful, and as signs and portents. Isa. 8:18: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me are for signs and wonders in Israel [הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי יהוה לאתות ולמופתים בישראל]. Christ the mediator and his elect disciples were portents in Israel, because of deeds such as never were seen, and because of words, since a man never spoke as he did, that is, so as to strike the conscience.

units.la: XVIII. Evidentissimè igitur patet, neque necessarium esse, neque Scripturis consentaneum, rationem, conditionem, aut qualitatem praerequisitam in homine statuere quasi objectum praedestinationis, ut Pontificii & Lutherani faciunt, hi fidem praevisam, illi opera bona, Praedestinanti Deo objicientes. Rom.9.16. οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος, ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος Θεοῦ. Non est volentis, neque currentis, sed gratificantis Dei. h.e. Praedestinatio adeóque electio, non perficitur hominum 1. voluntate, h.e. fide, & consilio. 2. Cursu, h.e. opere, sed gratiâ & misericordiâ Dei, atque ita ex vocante τοῦ μὴ ὄντος ὡς ὄντας, qui vocat ea quae non sunt, tanquam sint, h.e. praedestinante, h.e. eligente, & reprobante eos, qui non sunt, ut sint, ita ut praedestinatio h.e. electio, & reprobatio, nihil aliud sit, quàm decretum Dei, quo vult esse rem, quae non est, h.e. electos & reprobos, qui non fuerunt, vult ut sibi appareant.
units.tr: XVIII. It is therefore most evident that it is neither necessary nor consistent with Scripture to set down some reason, condition, or quality required in man as the object of predestination, as the Papists and the Lutherans do, the latter putting foreseen faith, the former good works, before the predestinating God. Rom. 9:16: "It is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy" [οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος, ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος Θεοῦ]. That is, predestination, and therefore election, is not accomplished, first, by the will of men, that is, by faith and counsel; second, by the running, that is, by works, but by the grace and mercy of God. Thus it is by him who calls the things that are not as though they were [τοῦ μὴ ὄντος ὡς ὄντας], that is, by him who predestines, that is, elects and reprobates those who are not, so that they may be; so that predestination, that is, election and reprobation, is nothing other than the decree of God by which he wills that a thing which is not should be, that is, he wills that the elect and the reprobate, who did not exist, should appear to him.

units.la: XIX. Hic verò in doctissimorum censuram Theologorum transfire non licet, qui, ut varii, ita varie de objecto divinae praedestinationis statuentes, utut sua, quaecunque tandem illa fuerint, distortâ Scripturâ (aliàs de homine jam lapso loquente) in suos in hoc arcano conceptus, quibus tamen hic indulgere non licebat, demonstrare conarentur, nihilominùs de infinito disputabant, mentémque suam quodammodò infinitam esse autumabant, dum ad ea, quae non intelligebant, extendebant. Nos certè ab Apostolo edocti φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν, sapere ad modestiam. Ut à revelatis non recedimus; ea enim nostra, & sola sunt, ad credendum, & faciendum: sic si quid occulti, aut arcani sit, tùm in horum, quae nobis revelata sunt, naturâ, modô, ordine, ac circumstantiis, tùm praeterea, id totum Deo, modestè relinquimus, & de infinito ultra Scripturam de hoc nihil determinantem non disputamus. Sed cum Confessione tutò pronunciamus, Deum praedestinâsse homines sine ullo eorum respectu, h.e. caeteris paribus (ut ego asequor[?]) (etiam) nullum hominis statum esse determinandum, si verò ita sit, nullum hic esse assignandum, ut reliqui excludantur; sufficit enim intelligere homines, inter se fuisse pares, ita ut differentia decreti non pendeat ex homine; differentia illa, quae in hominibus reperitur, ex decreto illo consequatur.
units.tr: XIX. Here, however, we may not go into the judgment of the most learned theologians, who, as they differ, so differ in determining the object of divine predestination. Whatever their own opinions were, they tried to demonstrate them by twisting Scripture (which speaks of fallen man) to fit their own notions on this mystery, though here they were not permitted to indulge such notions. Nonetheless they disputed about the infinite and thought their minds were in some way infinite, since they extended them to things they did not understand. We, however, taught by the Apostle to think so as to be sober-minded [φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν], to be wise unto sobriety. We do not depart from what has been revealed, for those things are ours, and they alone, for believing and doing. So if anything is hidden or secret, whether in the nature, mode, order and circumstances of the things revealed to us, or beyond that, we modestly leave all of it to God, and we do not dispute about the infinite beyond Scripture, which determines nothing about this. But when we state with confidence, with the Confession, that God predestined men without any regard to them, that is, other things being equal (as I understand it), no state of man is to be determined. And if that is so, no particular state is to be assigned here so that the rest are excluded. For it is enough to understand that men were equal among themselves, so that the difference in the decree does not depend on man; that difference which is found among men follows from the decree.

units.la: XX. Quod verò ad tertium, nempe aeternitatem electionis attinet, eam Confessio probat ex Epistola Sancti Pauli ad Ephes. 1.4. Elegit nos antequam jacerentur fundamenta mundi h.e. ab aeterno. [illegible, ~5 letters]
units.tr: XX. As for the third point, namely the eternity of election, the Confession proves it from Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians 1:4: "He chose us before the foundation of the world," that is, from eternity. [illegible, about five letters]

units.la: Praelegit nos in ipso ante fundamentamundi. Elegit nos (sibi) In ipso ante principia mundi. Sed cur æternitatem hujus consilii hac phrasi declaret, causa est; quia fundatio mundi, adeóque terræ, subordinatur decreto electionis, & ad id respectum habet. Quem respectum in his ponimus. I. Creationem mundi esse effectum æterni decreti electionis. 1. Q. David Pf. 136. v. 5-9. creationem cœli, & terræ fundationem, distinctionem diei, & noctis, ejusque gubernationem, hujus per lunam, & stellas ad tenebrarum moderationem; illius, per solem, cujus cursu dierum efficitur differentia in annua periodo, ut sint καιροὶ καιροφόροι in toto orbe; ad gratiam refert. Et bene; quia absoluta creatione, dum Deus, Adamum & Evam in horto collocâsset, eósque legi subjecisset, in qua non manserunt, sed lapsi sunt, statim loquutus est de gratia. Quæ ratio agendi indicat Deum, hæc omnia fecisse ad demonstrationem gratiæ in peccatore, atque adeò gratiam esse æternam, & antecedere jacta mundi fundamenta. 2. Q. Deus in creatione mundi, voluit per cœlum, & terram narrari gloriam suam. Alioqui enim illa frustra condidisset. Ideò & terram voluit inhabitari ab hominibus Jef. 45. 17. 18. Sic ait Jehova, qui creavit cœlum, is est Deus, qui formavit terram, & perfecit eam, is eam aptavit. Non incassum creavit eam, ad habitandum formavit eam, & inter homines habere populum qui gloriam ipsius enarret Jef. 41. 1. 3. 4. Nam nisi sint, qui quærant Deum, qui credant in Deum, nemo erit cui cœlum enarret gloriam Dei: Nam nemo infidelium curat Deum Psal. 14; verf. 1. 4. 5. Q. Quis credat, Deum voluisse hoc, ut terra ex abyssô emergat, expansum in sublime extendatur hoc fine, ut terra tantum à malis, & ingratis hominibus calcaretur, & cœlum spectaretur à brutis? Solis igitur electis lucet Sol, & stellæ, ipsis currunt dies, ac noctes, menses, & anni. Facit quidem Deus solem oriri super malos, æque ac bonos; sed revera ipsis sol, & si oriatur non lucet; quia molitionem Domini non aspiciunt, & opus manuum ejus non vident. Soli etiam electi sunt hæredes mundi à Deo creati, soli habent justum domini titulum, reliqui non sunt legitimi possessores; sed tantum usurpatores. II. Creationem seu formationem electorum, non esse simpliciter ab imperio Dei; sed à gratia, & amore electionis. Non igitur 1. communis providentiæ, gratiæ, & amoris signum est eorum creatio. 2. Neq; est eadem cum creatione, & formatione reproborum; horum enim est ab imperio, & potentia, illorum verò etiam à gratia. Nisi hæc ita sint, nescio quid ponderis habebit oratio Judæorum fidelium. Apud Esaiam cap. 64; 7. 8. Jobi, cap. 10 v. 3, petita à creatione, præ oratione reproborum: Sic orant Judæi [Hebrew: ועתה יהוה אבינו אתה אנחנו החמר ואתה יצרנו
units.tr: "He foreloved us in him before the foundation of the world; he chose us (for himself) in him before the beginnings of the world." But the reason why he declares the eternity of this counsel by this phrase is that the founding of the world, and so of the earth, is subordinate to the decree of election and has regard to it. We place this regard in the following. I. The creation of the world is the effect of the eternal decree of election. 1. David, Ps. 136:5-9, refers the creation of heaven, the founding of the earth, the distinction of day and night, and their governance (the latter by the moon and stars to regulate the darkness, the former by the sun, whose course makes the difference of days in the annual cycle, so that there are seasons bearing seasons [καιροὶ καιροφόροι] throughout the world) to grace. And rightly so, for when God had completed the creation and placed Adam and Eve in the garden and subjected them to the law, in which they did not remain but fell, he at once spoke of grace. This manner of acting shows that God made all these things to demonstrate grace toward the sinner, and so grace is eternal and precedes the laying of the foundations of the world. 2. God, in creating the world, willed that his glory be declared through heaven and earth; otherwise he would have made them in vain. Therefore he also willed the earth to be inhabited by men, Isa. 45:17-18: "Thus says the LORD, who created the heavens, he is God, who formed the earth and made it, he has established it. He did not create it in vain; he formed it to be inhabited, and to have among men a people who will declare his glory." Isa. 41:1, 3, 4: For unless there are those who seek God, who believe in God, there will be no one to whom the heavens declare the glory of God; for none of the unbelievers cares for God (Ps. 14:1, 4, 5). Question: who would believe that God willed this, that the earth should rise out of the abyss and be spread out on high for this end, that the earth should be trodden only by evil and ungrateful men, and heaven be gazed upon by brutes? The sun and the stars shine, then, only for the elect; for them the days, nights, months and years run their course. God indeed makes the sun rise on the evil as well as the good; but in truth the sun does not shine for them, even when it rises, because they do not regard the work of the Lord and do not see the deeds of his hands. The elect alone are the heirs of the world created by God; they alone have the just title of lordship; the rest are not lawful possessors but only usurpers. II. The creation or formation of the elect is not simply from the command of God, but from the grace and love of election. Therefore their creation is not 1. a sign of common providence, grace and love. 2. Nor is it the same as the creation and formation of the reprobate; for theirs is from command and power, but the elect's is also from grace. Unless these things are so, the prayer of the faithful Jews, drawn from creation, will have little weight, in contrast with the prayer of the reprobate. In Isaiah 64:7-8 and Job 10:3 the Jews pray thus: [Hebrew: ועתה יהוה אבינו אתה אנחנו החמר ואתה יצרנו

units.la: ומעשה ידיך כלנו אל תקצף יהוה עד מאד ואל לעד תזכר עון [?] הבט נא עמך כלנוEt nunc ô Domine Tu es Pater noster. Nos argilla, Tu figulus es, opus manuum tuarum sumus omnes nos. Ne effervescas summè, neque in perpetuum recorderis delictum. Ecce intuere populus tuus sumus omnes nos. Job sic: הודיעני על מה תריבני הטוב לך כי תעשק כי תמאס יגיע כפיך ועל עצת רשעים הופעתNotifica mihi cur mecum litiges. Num bonum tibi, ut opprimas? ut spernas laborem manuum tuarum. Et ad consilium improborum alluceres?
units.tr: ומעשה ידיך כלנו אל תקצף יהוה עד מאד ואל לעד תזכר עון [?] הבט נא עמך כלנו] "And now, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, you are the potter, and we are all the work of your hands. Do not be exceedingly angry, O LORD, nor remember iniquity forever. Behold, look, we are all your people." [Hebrew as above] Job says: "Make known to me why you contend with me. Is it good for you to oppress, to despise the labour of your hands and to shine upon the counsel of the wicked?" [הודיעני על מה תריבני הטוב לך כי תעשק כי תמאס יגיע כפיך ועל עצת רשעים הופעת]

units.la: XXI. Fundatio igitur terræ indicium est Dei jam ante regnum gratiæ meditantis, & populum sibi, qui laudem suam enarret, formantis. Conf.
units.tr: XXI. The founding of the earth, therefore, is a sign that God, even before the kingdom of grace, was meditating on it and forming a people for himself to declare his praise. Conf.

units.la: Apoc.1 3: 8.
units.tr: Apoc. 1 3: 8.

units.la: XXII. Quamvis autem nullum fuerit meritum, propter quod Deus Sanctos prædestinavit; tamen non sine medio elegit; sed in Christo, & propter Christum, ut qui jam sunt in Christo insiti per fidem, ipsi etiam sint electi, extra Christum reprobi. Probat hoc confessio. 2. Cor. 1 3: 5. ἑαυτὰς πειράζετε, εἰ ἐστὲ ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε, ἢ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν; εἰ μήτι ἀδόκιμοί ἐστε. h. e. inquirite in pignus electionis veštræ, in fidem, h.e. num acquiescatis in Deo, ut peccatori bono, authore salutis æternæ, & se quærentibus remunerante? nisi enim fidem habeatis, in Christo non estis, atque ita reprobi comperiemini.
units.tr: XXII. Although there was no merit on account of which God predestined the Saints, yet he did not choose them without a means; rather, he chose them in Christ and on account of Christ, so that those who are already grafted into Christ through faith should themselves be elect, while those outside Christ are reprobate. The Confession proves this from 2 Corinthians 13:5: "Examine yourselves, whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Or do you not know yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless indeed you are reprobate" [ἑαυτὰς πειράζετε, εἰ ἐστὲ ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἑαυτοὺς δοκιμάζετε, ἢ οὐκ ἐπιγινώσκετε ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν; εἰ μήτι ἀδόκιμοί ἐστε]. That is: inquire into the pledge of your election, into faith, that is, whether you rest in God as the good giver of eternal salvation and rewarder of those who seek him. For unless you have faith, you are not in Christ, and so you will be found reprobate.

units.la: XXIII. Elegit itaque nos Deus in Christo, & propter Christum h.e. uno actu, uno decreto, & quidem eodem, quo decrevit cœlum & terram condere, & hanc fundare, nos, & Christum elegit. Christus enim dicitur προεγνωσμένῳ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, pracognitus ante fundationem mundi.
units.tr: XXIII. God therefore chose us in Christ and on account of Christ, that is, by one act, one decree, and indeed the same decree by which he decreed to create heaven and earth and to found them. He chose us and Christ together. For Christ is called foreknown before the foundation of the world [προεγνωσμένου πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου], 1 Pet. 1:20, that is, chosen at the same time as we were.

units.la: 1. Pet. 1: 20. h. e. simul nobiscum electus. Elegit ergo 1 in Christo h.e. ut in capite; Christus enim primò fuit electus, ut caput, ac deinde homines quidam, ut membra in ipso, non quòd jam caput esset, & membra essemus; sed ut caput esset, & membra essemus. 2. Propter Christum, h.e. non ut Christus sit causa meritoria, vel impulsiva, respectu ipsius electionis hominum; sed ut causæ rationem habeat, respectu omnium effectorum electionis, quæ ipsius Christi missionem sequuntur. Quæritur igitur hic.
units.tr: Elect therefore 1. in Christ, that is, as in the head. For Christ was first chosen as the head, and then certain men as members in him, not because he was already the head and we were already the members, but so that he might be the head and we the members. 2. On account of Christ, that is, not so that Christ is the meritorious or impulsive cause of the election of men, with respect to the election itself; but so that he has the character of a cause with respect to all the effects of election, which follow the mission of Christ himself. The question therefore arises here.

units.la: Utrum, Christus sit causa meritoria electionis?
units.tr: Whether Christ is the meritorious cause of election?

units.la: In locum Sancti Pauli ad Ephes. cap. 1. v. 4. & 6. sæpiùs à Confessione citatum, dum legerem Magnum Theologum Johannem Crocium, in suo quem edidit in Epistolas Pauli minores Commentario, incidi in hæc verba. Sunt qui dicunt, elegisse in Christo, id est, ut per Christum tanquam mediatorem servaret, vel destinâsse ad salutem in Christo adipiscendam. Non eos damno, qui sic explicant, quia in eo fundamentum salutis tenent incolume, quod salutem fundent in solo Christo. Mihi tamen (NB) magis pla placet notare causam, propter quam Deus nos elegerit, ut sensus sit, nos elegit in Christo, id est, per, & propter Christum. Ut vero Vir Doctissimus suspicionem syncretismi cum Lutheranis amoveat, allegat pro se Confessionem Helveticam; dicit enim. Ut habet Confessio Helvetica: Ergo non sine medio, (NB) sed non propter ullum meritum; sed in Christo, & propter Christum elegit nos Deus. Ubi addit. Magni, tum inter Papistas, tum inter nos, Theologi, non electionem nostram, ex merito Christi praevisio; sed solam exequutionem factam esse docent. Atqui, inquit, Apostolus dicit diserte, Elegit nos in ipso, id est, Christo. Ergo non tantum exequutio electionis; sed & electio nostra propter Christum facta est. Verum, ad argumentum hoc nostri Theologi respondent, negando Consequentiam; Dicimur enim (inquiunt) in Christo electi, non quod ad electionem Deus fuerit permotus Christi merito; sed quod decreverit nos salvos facere in Christo; Itaque Christus non est causa decreti electionis; sed medium ad exequutionem electionis ab aeterno in ipsa electione destinatum, seu non est causa decreti; sed exequutionis decreti, in ipso tamen decreto quoque considerata. 1. Q. Scriptura S. nusquam electionem nostri a Christi merito arcessit, aut Christi morti ascribit, sicuti reconciliationem nostri, & salutis adeptionem ei ascribit; sed tantum gratiae; beneplacito, & misericordiae; quae esse unicum electionis nostrae fundamentum satis & nos astruximus. 2. Q. dilectio Dei, amor, & cura peculiaris erga electos, aperte anteponitur, merito ac morti Christi, imo traditionis Christi & crucifixionis in mortem causa dicitur Joh. 4: 10. In hoc est charitas, non quod nos dilexerimus Deum; sed quod ipse dilexit nos, & misit filium suum, propitiationem pro peccatis nostris. Unde necessario consequitur, dilectionem electorum ordine antecessisse in decreto Dei traditionem Christi in mortem, ac proinde traditionem Christi in mortem seu meritum Christi, non fuisse hujus dilectionis, atque electionis causam. Ita Magni Theologi, Walaeus, Wendelinus, Franciscus Burmannus. Sed pergit Vir Doctissimus, & dicit. Qui electi sunt, in Christo sunt electi, nemo extra Christum eligitur, Deus enim elegit nos in Christo h.l.v.4. Ergo meritum Christi hinc male excluditur, ille satisfecit Deo pro peccato, & effecit, ut posset peccatores, quos vellet, salva sua justitia eligere. Remove Christum & Deus est ignis consumens: Deut. 4:24. Ideo Helvetica, inquit, Ecclesia in Confessione priori cap. 10. Ergo, inquiunt, non sine medio; sed non propter ullum meritum; sed in Christo, & propter Christum. Hoc argumentum cum praecedenti idem est, ad quod etiam Nostri Theologi respondent. Ut ut nemo extra Christum eligatur; sed in Christo tamen meritum Christi non est causa electionis nostrae; quatenus est decretum & actus voluntatis Dei, prout Lutherani concipiunt; qui Christum causam electionis ipsius meritoriam statuunt; quam factam volunt intuitû meriti Christi,& propter ipsum: cùm non solùm actus ille voluntatis Dei,nullam causam externam,à qua moveatur admittat; sed & disertè Christus datus dicatur ex dilectione Dei erga homines Joh.7.v.16. ut jam ante Deus humanum genus dilexerit,& decretum electionis secerit,cujus exequendi Christus Minister destinatus est, & simul electus Dei servus Esa.42:1. qui electionem non praecedit ut causa; sed eam consequitur simul electus. Atque ita in ipso electi sumus Eph.1:4. h.e. in ipso benedicendi, & simul cum ipso,ut primogenito,& capite nostro,qui propterea Princeps salutis nostrae dicitur Hebr.2:10. Praecognitus ante jacta mundi fundamenta. 1.Petr.1:20. quique gratiae, ac gloriae nobis destinatae,causa meritoria est,& salutis nobis conficiendae summus auctor,& arbiter. Ita Magnus scripturarius Franciscus Burmannus. In synopsi Oeconomiae foederum Dei Part.1.c.38.§.24.
units.tr: On the passage of St Paul in Ephesians 1:4 and 6, which the Confession often cites, I was reading the great theologian John Crocius in his commentary on Paul's shorter Epistles, and I came upon these words: Some say that he chose us in Christ, that is, that he would preserve us through Christ as mediator, or that he destined us to obtain salvation in Christ. I do not condemn those who explain it this way, since they keep the foundation of salvation intact by grounding salvation in Christ alone. To me, however (NB), it pleases more to note the cause on account of which God chose us, so that the sense is: he chose us in Christ, that is, through and on account of Christ. But this most learned man, wishing to remove the suspicion of syncretism with the Lutherans, cites the Helvetic Confession in his support. For he says: As the Helvetic Confession has it: therefore not without a means, (NB) but not on account of any merit; but God chose us in Christ and on account of Christ. There he adds: the great theologians, both among the Papists and among us, teach that our election was not founded on the foreseen merit of Christ, but only that its execution was accomplished through him. Yet, he says, the Apostle plainly says, He chose us in him, that is, in Christ. Therefore not only the execution of election but our election itself was made on account of Christ. Our theologians, however, answer this argument by denying the consequence. For we are said (they say) to be chosen in Christ not because God was moved to election by the merit of Christ, but because he decreed to save us in Christ. Thus Christ is not the cause of the decree of election, but the means to its execution, destined from eternity within the election itself; or, he is not the cause of the decree but of the execution of the decree, though considered also within the decree itself. 1. Holy Scripture nowhere derives our election from the merit of Christ or ascribes it to his death, as it ascribes to him our reconciliation and the obtaining of salvation. It ascribes election only to grace, good pleasure and mercy, which we have sufficiently shown to be the sole foundation of our election. 2. The love of God, his special love and care for the elect, is plainly placed before the merit and death of Christ; indeed the handing over of Christ and his crucifixion to death is said to be caused by it: Joh. 4:10. In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as a propitiation for our sins. Whence it necessarily follows that the love of the elect preceded, in the order of God's decree, the handing over of Christ to death; and therefore the handing over of Christ to death, that is, the merit of Christ, was not the cause of this love and of election. So the great theologians Walaeus, Wendelinus and Franciscus Burmannus. But the most learned man goes on and says: Those who are elect are chosen in Christ; no one is chosen outside Christ, for God chose us in Christ (here, v. 4). Therefore the merit of Christ is wrongly excluded from this: he satisfied God for sin and so made it possible for God to elect, with his justice preserved, whichever sinners he wished. Remove Christ and God is a consuming fire: Deut. 4:24. Hence, he says, the Helvetic Church in the earlier Confession, chapter 10: therefore, they say, not without a means; but not on account of any merit; but in Christ and on account of Christ. This argument is the same as the preceding one, and our theologians answer it in the same way. Although no one is chosen outside Christ, nevertheless the merit of Christ is not, in Christ, the cause of our election, insofar as election is the decree and act of God's will. The Lutherans, who make Christ the meritorious cause of election itself, conceive it otherwise; they want it made in view of the merit of Christ and on account of it. For that act of God's will admits no external cause by which it might be moved. Moreover, Christ is expressly said to be given out of God's love towards men, John 7:16, so that God had already loved the human race and made the decree of election, whose execution Christ was destined to minister. At the same time he is the elect servant of God, Isa. 42:1, who does not precede election as its cause but follows it, being elected together with it. And so in him we are elect, Eph. 1:4, that is, blessed in him and together with him, as firstborn and our head; and for this reason he is called the Prince of our salvation, Heb. 2:10, foreknown before the foundation of the world, 1 Pet. 1:20; and he is the meritorious cause of the grace and glory destined for us, and the chief author and arbiter of the salvation to be accomplished for us. So the great scripturist Franciscus Burmannus, in the Synopsis of the Economy of God's Covenants, part 1, chapter 38, §24.

units.la: XXIV. Quod verò attinet verba Confessionis: propter Christum, à Magno Reformato Theologo pro se allegata,nostrum esse agnoscimus, ea à sensu isto alieno vindicare,& genuinum indicare. Nempe verba haec: propter Christum,praeter id quod statim praecedenti thesi ad initium diximus,dicimus etiam pactum Patris cum filio indigitare,quô scil.Pater filium in decreto electionis dedit redemptorem,pro certis quibusdam hominibus, & filius spospondit se expositurum animam suam satisfactionem. Ita ut sensus sit: Elegit nos in Christo h.e.ut in capite,& propter Christum h.e. non tantùm simpliciter ut caput nostrum esset; sed tale caput,quod etiam sponsor esset,& se ad ultimum usque quadrantem persolvendum sisteret. Quo respectu decretum electionis respectu Patris Electio, respectu filii sponsio rectissimè dicitur.
units.tr: XXIV. As for the words of the Confession, on account of Christ, which the great Reformed theologian cites in his support, we acknowledge that it is our task to vindicate them from that alien sense and to point out their genuine meaning. Besides what we said at the beginning of the immediately preceding thesis, we say that these words on account of Christ also indicate the covenant of the Father with the Son, by which the Father, in the decree of election, gave the Son as redeemer for certain men, and the Son promised that he would lay down his soul as satisfaction. So the sense is: he chose us in Christ, that is, as in our head, and on account of Christ, that is, not merely that he should be our head in a simple way, but such a head as would also be surety and would stand ready to pay to the last farthing. In this respect, the decree of election is most rightly called election with regard to the Father, and suretyship with regard to the Son.

units.la: XXV. Si verò quis nobis objiciat: Nos quidem bene facere, quòd verba Confessionis sic explicemus; sed videri confessionem statuere Christum esse causam meritoriam electionis;adeoq; nostram explicationem destitui authoritate,tùm Scripturae,tùm Confessionis. Respondemus, Authoritate scripturae nullo modo destitui,in posteriori parte disputationis Thesi 2. 3.4 &c. ostendemus. 2. Quod attinet authoritatem Confessionis, eâ planè ita sum confirmatus,ut nullo modo possim descendere ad hoc,ut verba,propter Christum,explicem de causa electionis meritoriâ. 1.Dico Confessionem nullo modo posse statuere istis verbis Christum esse causam meritoriam electionis, quia Confessio non potuit sui oblivisci;neq; id quod semel docuit evertere; docuit autem §1. Deum elegisse sanctos liberè,& merâ suâ gratiâ; Omnem igitur causam meritoriam, ipsum etiam Christum talis causae respectum habentem,exclusit.2. Verba Confessionis non sunt[?] extendenda ultra suum scopum,scopus autem est hoc articulo agere in solidum de medio electionis, oppositè ad non causam ejus, ideò dicit: Quamvis non propter meritum, non tamen sine medio..3. In Christo, & propter Christum Confessio explicat esse insitum Christo per fidem; fidem autem non constituit causam meritoriam electionis, ergo neque Christum potest .4. Phrasis: insitum esse Christo per fidem, qua explicat Confessio: electionem in Christo, & propter Christum ex mente Confessionis, vel refertur ad decretum electionis; vel ad exequutionem decreti electionis. Non prius. Quia per τὸ insitum esse Christo per fidem, distinguitur actu, & in se electus à reprobo, ut docet confessio; sed in mente Dei, seu in decreto praedestinationis, electus actu, & in se non distinguitur à reprobo. Q. praedestinatio, adeoque electio, nullam disparitatem internam facit in ipsis praedestinatis, ante applicationis actualem dispensationem; Praedestinatio enim adeoque electio, ante applicationem gratiae, nihil ponit in praedestinatis adeoque electis; sed latet in solo praedestinante, non enim id distinguit actu, in se se electum à reprobo; quod est in Deo, quale est decretum electionis; sed id quod est in ipso electo, quale est τὸ insitum esse Christo per fidem. Sic Paulus ab aeterno electus, nihilo aliis reprobis erat melior ante vocationem, & fidem in Christum. Relinquitur ergo phrasin illam referri ad exequutionem decreti electionis; & sic Confessionem Christum, non intentionis decreti electionis; sed exequutionis decreti electionis causam meritoriam constituere.
units.tr: XXV. If anyone objects to us that we explain the words of the Confession well in this way, but that the Confession seems to establish Christ as the meritorious cause of election, and so our explanation lacks the authority both of Scripture and of the Confession: we reply that it is by no means without the authority of Scripture, as we will show in the latter part of the disputation, in theses 2, 3, 4 and following. As for the authority of the Confession, I am so thoroughly persuaded of it that I cannot in any way come to explain the words on account of Christ as referring to a meritorious cause of election. 1. I say that the Confession cannot by any means mean, in these words, that Christ is the meritorious cause of election, because the Confession could not forget itself or overturn what it had once taught. It did teach, in §1, that God chose the saints freely and by his mere grace. It therefore excluded every meritorious cause, including Christ himself as having the character of such a cause. 2. The words of the Confession are not to be extended beyond their scope. Its scope in this article is to treat fully of the means of election, as opposed to its cause; therefore it says: although not on account of merit, yet not without a means. 3. The Confession explains in Christ and on account of Christ as being grafted into Christ through faith. But it does not make faith the meritorious cause of election, and therefore it cannot make Christ such a cause either. 4. The phrase being grafted into Christ through faith, by which the Confession explains election in Christ and on account of Christ, must, according to the mind of the Confession, refer either to the decree of election or to the execution of the decree of election. Not to the former. For the being grafted into Christ through faith ([τὸ] insitum esse Christo per fidem) distinguishes the elect, in act and in himself, from the reprobate, as the Confession teaches; but in the mind of God, or in the decree of predestination, the elect is not distinguished in act and in himself from the reprobate. Predestination, and therefore election, makes no internal difference in the predestined before the actual application of the dispensation of grace. Predestination, and hence election, before the application of grace, posits nothing in the predestined, and so in the elect; it lies hidden in God alone who predestines. For it does not distinguish the elect in act and in himself from the reprobate. What is in God, such as the decree of election, does not do this; what does it is what is in the elect person himself, such as being grafted into Christ through faith. Thus Paul, elected from eternity, was no better than the other reprobates before his calling and his faith in Christ. It remains, therefore, that the phrase refers to the execution of the decree of election; and so the Confession makes Christ the meritorious cause not of the intention of the decree of election, but of the execution of the decree of election.

units.la: XXVI. Neque igitur fides, neque opera bona, neque Christus est causa meritoria electionis; sed medium in ipso electionis decreto consideratum. Rom.8.29.30. Quantum ad fidem, eam Confessio ut summum mediorum agnoscit, & ponit: Ut qui jam sunt in Christo insiti per fidem, illi ipsi sint etiam electi. In Christo esse 1.Cor.1.30. Joh.17:21. est in ipsum credere & in ipsum credere, est in ipso esse, quod notat. I. Mori peccatis, reviviscere ad vitam, justitiam fieri; Charitas enim Christi, qua pro nobis mortuus est, ad hoc nos constringit, ut omnes moriamur peccato, revivificamus vitae, ut qui posthac, non nobis; sed ei qui pro nobis mortuus est, vivamus; 2.Cor.5:5. 1.Cor.15:22. Phil.3:9. 2.Cor.5:1.2. Nisi hoc sit, cum Christo, qui propterea ex mortuis resurrexit; ut se justificatum à peccatis imputatis, & nos justificantem ostenderet, denique ut resurrectionis nostrae, tum spiritualis, ex peccatis, tum corporalis ex sepulchro, hypostasis, exemplar, & initiatio fierer; nullam similitudinem habere, adeoque in ipso esse per fidem minime possumus. II. In ipso nos Deum benedicere, & gratia cumulari. Eph.1.3. Benedictus Deus, & Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui benedixit nos, in omni benedictione spirituali in coelestibus in Christo, hoc est ut principe salutis ut τελειωτὴν τῆς πίστεως consummatore fidei, ut ἀρχιερεῖ, ἐγγυῷ[?] & μεσίτῃ τῆς Διαθήκης. In Christo sunt omnes benedictiones spirituales in supercoelestibus. In Christo causa est ἁγιασμῷ & δικαιοσύνης, & vitae aeternae ad gloriam in corpore participandam. Q. Christus est semen illud,in quo benedicendæ erant omnes gentes,h.e. quemadmodum Christus morte suâ impetravit,& accepit dona,h.e. vocationem,justificationem, & glorificationem,electis hominibus elargienda: ita vicissim homines accipiunt in ipso. Ille in hominibus ut suis membris dona accipit, ut ipsorum vivificatio,& glorificatio ipsi debeatur,& ab ipso profluat. III. Nos collocari in supercœlestibus, seu in ipso nos sedere in cœlis. Eph. 2:6. Collocati sumus in supercœlestibus,h.e. dum Christus collocatus est in cœlis etiam nos cum illo in cœlis collocati sumus. Christus πρόδρομος ἡμῶν [?] pracursor noster, is caput: nos membra. Honor capitis est honor membrorum, Regnum capitis est regnum membrorum, πολίτευμα [?] noster in cœlis est, Hierosolyma illa nova in quam ascendimus instar aquilæ, neque amplius in pulvere,& humi instar stolidi struthionis nidulamur. IV. Per ipsum justos nos constitui Rom. 5: v. 19. [?] Ἀφ' ὥσπερ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί, Per unum hoc est, qui nempe neque cum Adamo peccavit; & in quem regnum peccati,& mortis non transfivit, qui dignus est, ut sit Dominus & caput,& novus Adam, origo & fons hæreditatis in fratres derivandæ. Obedientiam justi constituentur multi,h.e. vi & valore ejus obedientiæ fient populus hæreditas, sponsa, membra Christi,& cum ipso communionem habebunt,& per ipsum inculpati,sine macula & ruga coram Deo sistentur. V. Nos filios esse Gal. 3.26. πάντες γὰρ υἱοὶ Θεοῦ ἐστε διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Omnes filii Dei estis per fidem in Christo Iesu,h.e. omnibus vobis, quicunque creditis in nomen filii Dei, filius dedit potestatem hanc, ut fitis filii Dei, h.e. ut non amplius sitis sub pædagogo, qui vos educent,& præparent ad hoc, ut ad patrem vestrum digne accedatis; sed habetis hoc jus, ut tutò ad ipsum accedatis. Et quidem juxta illam Prophetiam. O cœli, cœli sunt Domini, terram autem dedit filiis hominum,h.e. vos qui tenetis summum in Ecclesia locum scitote cœlum h.e. Ecclesiam esse Domini,& terram dedisse filiis hominum h.e. ut omnes pari jure in Ecclesia tanquam fratres, ad Christum accedant,& cum ipso coram throno gratiæ ut filii appareant.
units.tr: XXVI. Therefore neither faith, nor good works, nor Christ is the meritorious cause of election; rather, it is a means considered within the decree of election itself. Rom. 8:29, 30. As for faith, the Confession acknowledges it as the chief of the means and states: That those who are now ingrafted into Christ through faith, they themselves may also be elect. To be in Christ (1 Cor. 1:30; John 17:21) is to believe in him, and to believe in him is to be in him, which is what the phrase signifies. I. To die to sins, to revive to life, to be made righteous. For the love of Christ, by which he died for us, constrains us to this: that we all die to sin and are made alive to life, so that from now on we live not for ourselves but for him who died for us (2 Cor. 5:15; 1 Cor. 15:22; Phil. 3:9; 2 Cor. 5:1, 2). Unless this is so, that is, unless we are with Christ, who for this reason rose from the dead, so that he might show himself justified from the sins imputed to him and us justified, and finally so that our resurrection, both spiritual from sins and bodily from the grave, might be made a substance, pattern and beginning, we could have no likeness to him, and so we could by no means be in him through faith. II. That in him we are blessed by God and heaped with grace. Eph. 1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ; that is, as the author of salvation, the perfecter of faith [τελειωτὴν τῆς πίστεως], as high priest, surety [ἐγγυῷ] and mediator of the covenant. In Christ are all spiritual blessings in the heavenly places. In Christ is the cause of sanctification [ἁγιασμῷ] and righteousness, and of eternal life, to be enjoyed in glory in the body. Q. Christ is that seed in whom all nations were to be blessed. That is, just as Christ by his death obtained and received gifts, namely calling, justification and glorification, to be bestowed on elect men, so in turn men receive them in him. He receives gifts in men as his members, so that their quickening and glorification are owed to him and flow from him. III. That we are placed in the heavenly places, or that in him we sit in the heavens. Eph. 2:6: We have been placed in the heavenly places; that is, since Christ has been placed in heaven, we also have been placed in heaven with him. Christ our forerunner [πρόδρομος] is the head, and we are the members. The honour of the head is the honour of the members, the kingdom of the head is the kingdom of the members. Our citizenship [πολίτευμα] is in heaven, in that new Jerusalem into which we ascend like eagles, and no longer nest in dust and on the ground like a foolish ostrich. IV. That through him we are made righteous. Rom. 5:19: [Ἀφ' ὥσπερ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί]: Through one, that is, one who neither sinned with Adam, and into whom the reign of sin and death did not pass, who is worthy to be Lord and head and the new Adam, the origin and source of the inheritance to be passed on to the brothers. By the obedience of one the many will be made righteous; that is, by the power and worth of that obedience they become a people, an inheritance, a bride, members of Christ, they will have communion with him, and through him they will stand before God blameless, without spot or wrinkle. V. That we are sons. Gal. 3:26: [πάντες γὰρ υἱοὶ Θεοῦ ἐστε διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ]: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus; that is, to all of you who believe in the name of the Son of God he has given this power, that you may be sons of God, that is, that you may no longer be under a tutor who leads you and prepares you to approach your father worthily, but you have this right, that you may approach him safely. And indeed this accords with that prophecy: O heavens, the heavens are the Lord's, but the earth he has given to the sons of men; that is, you who hold the highest place in the Church should know that the heaven, that is the Church, belongs to the Lord, and that the earth has been given to the sons of men, so that all, with equal right in the Church, as brothers, may come to Christ and appear with him before the throne of grace as sons.

units.la: XXVII. Ex quâ in Christo ex parte præexplicatâ (quis enim ditissimas beneficii divini venas homuncio in totum exhauriet?) existentiâ, infert Confessio eos esse electos, sicuti eos qui sunt extra Christum reprobos. Unicum enim hoc electionis signum reliqua includens, eum qui ab æterno secundùm propositum Dei fuit electus, facit ut in tempore suam sentiat electionem, vocatione accedente, quæ non tantùm est sollicitatio per mandatum fidei,& promissionem ei additam, contrariâmque comminationem; sed cordis ipsius compellatio,& commotio imò effectûs divini, divina in homine jussio,& potens hominis peccatoris, ad communionem Dei adductio, quæ communio est in Christo, per fidem autem sumus in Christo. Igitur vocatio est fidei largitio, qui fidem non habent, in Christo non sunt, Christo se gestandos committere non possunt, neque ipso ullo modo niti. Quare oportet eos esse extra Christum, hoc est, I. Mori in peccatis, ἐπιμένειν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ immanere peccato, hoc est affixos deditissimósque esse peccato. II. Nullis Christi beneficiis cumulari; si enim Christus pro ipsis traditus in mortem non est; neque etiam quicquam ex beneficiis à Christo partis ipsis communicatur. Quia communio beneficiorum Christi, ut vocationis, justificationis, adoptionis, sanctificationis, & glorificationis, pertinet tantum ad eos, pro quibus Christus à Patre traditus est, h.e. quos redemit; Applicatio enim beneficiorum Christi, ejusdem planè latitudinis est cum ipsa redemptione; quia finis redemptionis est ejus applicatio. III. Exulari cœlo & sancta Hierosolyma, h.e. nullum commeatum, nullam communionem cum Christo, & Ecclesia habere; sed cum mari, h.e. mundo à Deo alieno, & cum diabolo, mundum & reprobos suis ventis, & agitationibus turbante, perpetuò conversari. Sancta Hierosolyma est civitas sancta; quia in sanguine, & Spiritu Christi sanctificata est, in quam non intrabunt, qui eam polluunt, sed foris erunt, ut qui diabolum & falsum Deum dotârunt, et quorum amori omnia impenderunt. IV. Eos per Adamum peccatores, & injustos constitui, ἀφ' ἑνὸς τῆς παρακοῆς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν[?] οἱ πολλοί, hoc est, in ea sunt conditione, ut judicandum de ipsis sit, eos indignos esse communione Dei, quemadmodùm de Adamo judicatum est, quum ejectus est ex paradiso, in quo communionis cum Deo, adeóque vitæ Symbolum, mediante arbore vitæ continebatur. Arbor vitæ significabat eum, qui est vita hominum; edere ex ea significabat unionem, & communionem cum ipso obtinere. Cum igitur Adam expulsus est hortô, & separatus ab arbore vitæ, documentô ipsi fuit, omnes naturaliter ab ipso descendentes, ipsius inobedientiæ in æternum participes, ab unione, & communione Dei finaliter separatos esse. V. Servos esse peccati, & diaboli. Venit Christus ut lux in mundum; sed tenebræ eam lucem non assequutæ sunt, venit in mundum qui per ipsum factus est; sed prout mundus per ipsum factus eum non agnovit; ita neque recepit, & quia non recepit, neque jus filiationis ab eo accepit. Mundus igitur, & qui ex eo sunt, manserunt servi, verùm non justitiæ, ut per eam redderentur liberi; sed peccati, hoc est, qui non possunt amare Deum, aut eum velle esse, vel saltem talem esse qualis est, ut qui bonô delectatur, & malum abominatur; qui à peccato victi, & per legem sive jus Dei obnoxii facti diabolo, ad omnem seductionem & excæcationem, ac contaminationem, abalienati sunt à vita Dei, hoc est, perperam cogitant. Servus peccati, peccatum sibi herum facit; ut servus justitiæ justitiam. Justitia suum herum ducit eâ viâ, quâ Deus ut peccatori amabilis, à peccatore glorificatur; peccatum eâ, quâ non potest non peccare, & nihil potest nisi peccare, est enim δούλος[?] τῆς φθορᾶς, h.e. mentis, & voluntatis corruptæ mancipium.
units.tr: XXVII. From this existence in Christ, partly explained above (for who could exhaust the richest veins of the divine benefit with a puny man?), the Confession infers that those who are in Christ are elect, just as those who are outside Christ are reprobate. For this one sign of election, which includes all the rest, makes him who was elected from eternity according to the purpose of God perceive his election in time, when calling approaches. This calling is not merely a solicitation through the command of faith, with the promise added to it and the contrary threat; it is a summoning and stirring of the heart itself, indeed the effect of the divine act, a divine command in man and a powerful leading of the sinful man into communion with God, which communion is in Christ; but we are in Christ through faith. Therefore calling is the bestowal of faith. Those who do not have faith are not in Christ, cannot commit themselves to be carried by Christ, and cannot lean on him in any way. Hence they must be outside Christ, that is: I. To die in sins, to remain in sin [ἐπιμένειν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ], that is, to be fixed to sin and most devoted to it. II. To be loaded with none of the benefits of Christ. For if Christ was not delivered to death for them, neither is anything of the benefits of Christ shared with them. The communion of Christ's benefits, such as calling, justification, adoption, sanctification and glorification, pertains only to those for whom Christ was delivered up by the Father, that is, whom he redeemed. For the application of Christ's benefits has exactly the same extent as redemption itself, since the purpose of redemption is its application. III. To be exiled from heaven and the holy Jerusalem, that is, to have no passage or communion with Christ and the Church, but to live perpetually among the sea, that is, the world alien to God, and with the devil, who stirs up the world and the reprobate with its winds and agitations. The holy Jerusalem is the holy city because it has been sanctified in the blood and Spirit of Christ; into it will not enter those who defile it, but they will remain outside, as those who have endowed the devil and a false God, and to whose love they have devoted everything. IV. That through Adam they are constituted sinners and unjust. Rom. 5:19: [ἀφ' ἑνὸς τῆς παρακοῆς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν]: Through the disobedience of one man the many were made sinners; that is, they are in such a condition that it must be judged of them that they are unworthy of communion with God, just as it was judged of Adam when he was cast out of paradise, where the pledge of communion with God, and thus of life, was contained by means of the tree of life. The tree of life signified him who is the life of men; eating from it signified obtaining union and communion with him. Therefore when Adam was driven out of the garden and separated from the tree of life, he was shown that all who descend from him naturally, sharing forever in his disobedience, are finally separated from union and communion with God. V. To be slaves of sin and of the devil. Christ came as light into the world, but the darkness did not grasp that light; he came into the world, which was made through him, yet as the world, though made through him, did not know him, so neither did it receive him, and because it did not receive him, it did not receive from him the right of sonship. The world, therefore, and those who are of it, remained slaves, but not slaves of righteousness, through which they might be made free; they were slaves of sin. That is, they cannot love God or wish him to be, or at least to be such as he is, one who delights in good and abominates evil. Conquered by sin, and made liable to the devil through the law or right of God, they are alienated from the life of God, and given over to every seduction, blindness and defilement; that is, they think perversely. The slave of sin makes sin his master, as the slave of righteousness makes righteousness his master. Righteousness leads its master by that way by which God, as lovable to the sinner, is glorified by the sinner; sin leads its slave by that way by which he cannot but sin, and can do nothing but sin, for he is a slave [δούλος] of corruption, that is, a bondsman of a corrupted mind and will.

units.la: XXVIII. Electi igitur, qui sunt per fidem in Christo, respectu illius unionis, rectissimè dicuntur esse in Christo, tanquam palmites in vite, h.e. manent in vite, Christo, fructum ferentes multum, & vitis Christus [Hebrew, ~1 word: מפרה?] frugiferos faciens palmites in ipsis. Reprobi verò, qui sunt extra Christum, veram illam vitem, sunt vepres, labruscæ, lentes, carnes legi Dei subjici nescia, seminantes carnisuæ, & ex illa interitum sibi metentes. Ipsi etiam hypocritæ fures, & lupi inter agnos Dei, Christo mentientes; sunt metæ diaboli genituræ, quos sibi similes genuit; prout enim ipse se transformat in Angelum lucis, & cum filiis Dei, ad thronum ejus iterato subsistit: ita isti in Ecclesia Dei nomen Christi præ se ferunt, & ex [Hebrew, ~1 word: לבוש?] communionem cum sanctis colunt; non sunt tamen palmites in vite h.e. non habent communionem cum Christo, qui est vera vitis, in qua fideles habent commeatum Spiritûs, & vitæ, & in quo etiam fructificant Joh. 15:1.2. Sed sunt palmites cum vite, h.e. stolones steriles, nomen tantum Christo dantes, infrugiferi, qui materiæ tenus viti adhærescunt quidem; verùm Spiritûs, vitæque participes non sunt; sed vitam in nomine, non in fructûs effectu ostentantes, solis pampinis, & foliis, iisque non ad sanationem gentium, luxuriant.
units.tr: XXVIII. The elect, then, who are through faith in Christ, are rightly said to be in Christ, with respect to that union, as branches are in the vine: that is, they remain in the vine, Christ, bearing much fruit, and Christ the vine making the branches in them fruitful. The reprobate, however, who are outside Christ, the true vine, are brambles, wild vines, thorns, and flesh that is not subject to the law of God, sowing to its own flesh and reaping destruction from it. Hypocrites too, thieves and wolves among the lambs of God who lie to Christ, are the offspring of the devil, whom he has begotten as like himself. For just as he transforms himself into an angel of light and again takes his place among the sons of God before his throne, so these people in the Church of God bear the name of Christ and, clothed in the appearance of communion with the saints, cultivate it. Yet they are not branches in the vine, that is, they have no communion with Christ, who is the true vine, in whom the faithful receive the inflow of the Spirit and of life, and in whom they also bear fruit (John 15:1, 2). They are rather branches with the vine, that is, barren shoots that give Christ only a name, unfruitful. They cling to the vine in outward substance, but they do not share in the Spirit and life. They display life in name, not in the effect of fruit, and they flourish only in leaves and foliage, and that not for the healing of the nations.

units.la: XXIX. Quemadmodùm autem electionis media dantur alia, præter unionem cum Christo, ut justificatio, adoptio &c. ab ea tamen ut plurimùm promanantia: ita etiam reprobationis, præter æternam à Christo separationem, dantur alia media, ut permissio peccati, derelictio in peccato, obduratio, (de qua supra th. XIII. obiter) punitio. Et qualesnam, & quantas tenebras eos manere necesse est, quibus Christus, Sol justitiæ, nunquam exortus est! Sed quia Confessio ista non urget, nos quoque in ista arena nimium non desudamus.
units.tr: XXIX. Just as there are other means of election besides union with Christ, such as justification, adoption, and so on, which for the most part flow from it, so also there are other means of reprobation besides eternal separation from Christ: permission of sin, abandonment in sin, hardening (of which above, thesis XIII, in passing), and punishment. And what and how great the darkness must be for those on whom Christ, the Sun of righteousness, has never risen! But since this Confession does not press the point, we too will not sweat too much in this arena.

units.la: XXX. § 3. Confessio finem electionis docet. Denique electi sunt sancti in Christo per Deum ad finem certum, quem & ipsum exponit Apostolus Eph. 1:4. 5. Elegit nos in ipso, ut essemus sancti, & irreprehensibiles coram illo per charitatem, qui prædestinavit nos, ut adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in sese, ut laudetur gloria gratiæ suæ. Finis autem ille certus est, vel eligentis Dei, vel Electorum. Electorum est i. Sanctitas, (seu sanctificatio. 2. Adoptio, ex quibus promanat finis eligentis; nimirum laus gloriæ gratiæ Dei.
units.tr: XXX. § 3. The Confession teaches the end of election. Finally, the elect are saints in Christ, through God, to a certain end, which the Apostle himself sets out (Eph. 1:4, 5): He chose us in him, that we should be holy and blameless before him in love; he who predestined us to adopt us as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, to the praise of the glory of his grace. This certain end is either the end of the electing God or the end of the elect. The end of the elect is (1) holiness (or sanctification), and (2) adoption. From these flows the end of the electing God, namely, the praise of the glory of God's grace.

units.la: XXXI. Quantum ad sanctificationem, dicit, ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ, εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους· καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ. h.e. decretum electionis est dilectio æterna, ad dandum uti vitam; ita & pietatem. Ergo electi sumus in Christo per fidem. 1. Ut repurgemur à peccatis nostris, per sanguinem Christi, & regeneremur ad votum melioris vitæ. 2. Ut simus sancti, h.e. ut voluntas nostra sit sancta, cor purum, omne studium in bona conscientia ad charitatem Dei, & proximi. 3. Ut simus irreprehensibiles, h.e.ut tanquam reprobi,à Christo,& justitiâ Dei alieni,coargui nequeamus; quia scil. omnes electi tales demum sunt in Christo, qui æternam in Christo electionem suâ sanctitate testantur. Et certè hæc nostra debet esse gratitudo erga Christum Redemptorem, necoram tribunali Patris sui, cùm ipsi tradet regnum, h. e. electos, quos Pater ipsi dedit redimendos, repræsentat Patri suo, & tradit jam Redemptos, cogatur nos abnegare. Matth.7.23.ut tales qui pudori sumus Deo, & sanctis, Esa.29 22.
units.tr: XXXI. As to sanctification, he says: he chose us in him, that we should be holy and without blemish before him in love [ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ, εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους· καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ]. That is, the decree of election is eternal love, given for the sake of life, and so also for godliness. Therefore we are elect in Christ through faith: (1) that we may be cleansed from our sins through the blood of Christ and be regenerated to the desire of a better life; (2) that we may be holy, that is, that our will may be holy, our heart pure, and our whole zeal, in a good conscience, directed to the love of God and of our neighbour; (3) that we may be blameless, that is, that as if we were reprobate, alien to Christ and to the righteousness of God, we could not be accused. For all the elect are at last such in Christ, who bear witness by their holiness to their eternal election in Christ. And surely this must be our gratitude toward Christ the Redeemer, lest, when he hands over the kingdom to his Father, he presents to his Father the elect, whom the Father gave him to redeem, and hands them over as already redeemed, and we be compelled to deny him (Matt. 7:23), so that we may not be shameful before God and the saints (Isa. 29:22).

units.la: XXXII. De Adoptione
units.tr: XXXII. On Adoption

units.la: dicit, προορίσας ἡμᾶς[?] εἰς υἱοθεσίαν[?] διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ εἰς αὐτὸν εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ[?], h.e. quos elegit Deus ad sanctificationem, eos etiam prædestinavit ad adoptionem, h.e. non tantum elegit ut essent sancti, & inculpati; sed etiam sanctitatis præmiū ex gratia ipsis destinavit, nimirum filiorum dignitatem. Sumus ergo filii, & hæredes Dei, h.e. 1. à Deo geniti, similes Deo, ut qui noscimus mysteria Patris, faciem ejus videmus, & ad eum in libertate, & fiducia, ut decet filios, accedimus.
units.tr: He says: having predestined us to adoption through Jesus Christ, to himself, to the praise of the glory of his grace [προορίσας ἡμᾶς εἰς υἱοθεσίαν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς αὐτὸν εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ]. That is, those whom God chose for sanctification, he also predestined to adoption. That is, he did not merely choose that they should be holy and blameless; he also appointed for them, out of grace, the reward of holiness, namely the dignity of sons. We are therefore sons and heirs of God, that is, (1) begotten by God, made like God, since we know the mysteries of the Father, see his face, and approach him in freedom and confidence, as sons should.

units.la: 2. Sumus domini omnium jure electionis in peculium, & quidem sanguine emendum, ipsius etiam Dei, jure communionis, & fœderis perpetui eo fruendi. Ita ut quemadmodum nos jure electionis sumus hæreditas Dei: ita Deus & Christus nostra est hæreditas. Unde iterum consequitur, hæreditatem Dei esse etiam nostram hæreditatem, & Regnum Dei esse etiam regnum nostrum.
units.tr: (2) We are lords of all things by the right of election, into a peculiar possession, and indeed to be possessed at the price of blood; we also enjoy God himself by the right of communion and of an everlasting covenant. So just as we are God's inheritance by the right of election, so God and Christ are our inheritance. Hence it follows again that the inheritance of God is also our inheritance, and the kingdom of God is also our kingdom.

units.la: XXXIII. Finis autem Dei eligentis in electione, est gloria gratia sua, quæ δόξα talis est, ut adjunctam habeat laudem ἔπαινον, h.e. testimonium rectitudinis, & virtutis divinæ in conscientiis electorum. Elegit ergo Deus nos in Christo, ut secundum electionem, ante jacta mundi fundamenta factam, simus sancti in conspectu ejus, in charitate, filii, & hæredes ejus, ut secundum propositum, quo decrevit ut celebraretur, & laudaretur sua gratia, eam celebraremus, & laudaremus. Quod si igitur talis gratia est in Deo, & Deus eam voluit celebrari, & laudari, consequitur, nos, qui sumus sancti, & fideles in Christo Jesu, posse, & debere Deo benedicere, qui nos elegit in peculium, & thesaurum, quem non prodiget; sed quo se in æternum glorificabit. Dicamus ergo: Dignus es Domine, qui accipias gloriam & honorem, & potentiam, quia tu condidisti omnia, & propter voluntatem tuam sunt, & condita sunt. Dignus es Domine, ut accipias benedictionem, quia emisti nos tibi in populum, fecisti nos reges, & sacerdotes, & regnabimus tecum. Tua sit igitur benedictio, honor, gloria, & imperium in sæcula sæculorum; Quia divitias gratiæ tuæ, tuam denique ad justificandum nos peccatores sufficientiam, prout ab æterno declarare, ostendere voluisti; ita in tempore, in nobis peccatoribus fecisti, declarasti, ostendisti.
units.tr: XXXIII. The end of God electing in election is the glory of his grace, which glory [δόξα] is such that it has joined to it praise [ἔπαινος], that is, the testimony of the rectitude and divine virtue in the consciences of the elect. God therefore chose us in Christ, that according to the election made before the foundation of the world we should be holy in his sight, in love, sons and heirs of him; and that according to the purpose by which he decreed that his grace should be celebrated and praised, we should celebrate and praise it. If then such grace is in God, and God willed it to be celebrated and praised, it follows that we, who are holy and faithful in Christ Jesus, can and ought to bless God, who chose us as a peculiar people and a treasure, which he will not squander, but in which he will glorify himself for ever. Let us say therefore: You are worthy, Lord, to receive glory and honour and power, because you created all things, and by your will they are and were created. You are worthy, Lord, to receive blessing, because you have bought us for yourself as a people, made us kings and priests, and we shall reign with you. Therefore let blessing, honour, glory, and dominion be yours for ages of ages; because the riches of your grace, and finally your sufficiency to justify us sinners, which you willed to declare and show from eternity, so you have in time made, declared, and shown in us sinners.

units.la: XXXIV. Quandoquidem certum est, quosdam ab æterno esse electos ad vitam æternam; quosdam vero reprobatos, sive neglectos. Quid judicandum de singulis hominibus? Respondet Confessio §.4. Bene sperandum est de omnibus (scil. singillatim sumptis, neque temere reprobis quisquam est annumerandus. Dicimus singillatim. Nam collective de omnibus non possumus bene judicare; quia novimus contrarium à Deo statutum. Id Confessio probat exemplo Pauli. Phil. 1.3.6.7. Qui oravit, & gratias egit pro tota Ecclesia Philippensi, in qua sine dubio potuerunt esse multi hypocritæ, adeoque reprobi, de quibus tamen bene sperabat, & judicabat, inquiens: Gratias ago pro vobis omnibus (loquitur autem de tota Ecclesia Philippensi) quod veneritis in communionem Evangelii persuasum habens, quod is, qui coepit opus bonum in vobis, perficiet, sicut justum est, ut hoc sentiam de vobis omnibus. Justum est; quia (ut pius Theologus Amesius inquit) charitati consentaneum est, de singulis optime judicare: quamvis collective de omnibus non liceat pronunciare, Christum ex aquo eorum causam apud Deum egisse. Q. nullus est quoad nos, qui non est, vel non potest esse particeps nobiscum ejusdem bonitatis divinæ, quamobrem etiam sigillatim pro omnibus orandum est.
units.tr: XXXIV. Since it is certain that some have been elected from eternity to eternal life, and some reprobated, or passed over, what is to be judged about individual men? The Confession, § 4, answers: Good hope is to be had of all (that is, taken singly), nor is anyone to be rashly numbered among the reprobate. We say singly, for we cannot judge well of all collectively, since we know that the opposite has been decreed by God. The Confession proves this by the example of Paul (Phil. 1:3, 6, 7), who prayed and gave thanks for the whole Philippian Church, in which without doubt there could be many hypocrites, and so reprobates, yet of whom he nevertheless had good hope and judged well, saying: I give thanks for you all (he speaks of the whole Philippian Church) that you have come into the fellowship of the gospel, being persuaded that he who began a good work in you will complete it, as it is right that I should think this of you all. It is right, because (as the pious theologian Amesius says) it is consistent with charity to judge well of each individual, although we may not pronounce collectively about all, since Christ equally pleaded their cause before God. For nobody is, as far as we are concerned, who is not, or cannot be, a partaker with us of the same divine goodness; for which reason everyone must also be prayed for individually.

units.la: Prout igitur neminem viventium in particulari debemus, ut neque possumus rejicere ab orationis nostræ communione, propter conjecturas, aut probabilia signa reprobationis; ita etiam temere reprobis nullus à nobis est annumerandus. Dicimus conjecturas, & signa probabilia reprobationis, quæ nulla dantur certa sicut electionis. Quæritur ergo hic. An ergo reprobatio in hac vita non est certa reprobis; sicuti electio certa est? Non est. Audi hic severum pietatis exactorem, doctrinâ & vitâ Theologum: Georgium Martonfalvi Transylvanum, inter Theologos Hungariæ Aquilam, per omnem meam ætatem in Patria, unicum Theologum Præceptorem, in doctissima suâ concione, de reprobationis incertitudine ita scribentem: Certum est, ex aquo omnium causam Christum apud Deum non egisse, neque pro mundo orâsse, tamen Deus certitudinem reprobationis sibi reservare voluit, & prout clemens, & misericors est, ne ipsis quidem reprobis significare voluit; si enim hoc reprobi scirent, ut ipsis diabolis saviores, crudeliores, mundum hactenus subvertissent, desperâssent, enormia quaque perpetrâssent, & ipsi electi propter eorum ferociam, mundo exire coacti fuissent. Ita aut forte non ultima causa, cur Deus eos celare voluit, sunt electi, propter quos etiam dies angustiarum, & afflictionum, teste Christo Domino, abbreviantur. Et si vel maxime reprobatio in hac vita reprobis certa esset, fieret hoc, vel ex peccato in S. Sanctum quod cadit solum in reprobos, quamvis non omnes; vel ex contrariis eorum, quibus electi de sua electione certi sunt; vel ex desperatione de divina misericordia: sed peccatum in S. Sanctum non potest ipsis esse certum signum reprobationis; nisi etiam sciant, se in peccatum illud incidisse, quod nemo unquam reproborum de se fatetur; q. omnes homines, & etiam reprobi eo sunt ingenio, ut non male de sesemetipsis sentiant. Neque etiam ex contrariis eorum, quibus electi certi redduntur de sua electione: quia illa omnia communia sunt electis nondum renatis, & certo tempore ad Ecclesiam adducendis. Desperandi vero causam de gratia & misericordia Dei, nemo reproborum in hac vita habere potest, nisi ipsi constet, quod Deus ipsum non velit participem facere gratiæ suæ, quod, quia raro, aut nunquam ordinariis mediis alicui constat, ante hujus vitæ finem, idcirco nemo reproborum potest de misericordia Dei desperare. Si vero quis dicat, Nos infra sollicitè probare ex practico Syllogismo certitudinem electionis, & consequenter reprobationis; siquidem contrariorum contraria sint consequentia. Dicimus, Logicum istum canonem; ne in somnio quidem quicquam de electione, & reprobatione vidisse; proinde nos illum pro norma certitudinis non agnoscere; verùm hinc exulare jubemus. Ad rem dicimus: Ille, qui signis electionis contraria in se reperit, vitam suam emendandam promittit, quamvis id nunquam præster, & sic reprobationis suæ in hac vita incertus manebit.
units.tr: Just as we must not regard any living person individually as reprobate, and so cannot exclude anyone from the fellowship of our prayers on the basis of guesses or probable signs of reprobation, so too we must not count anyone among the reprobate rashly. We speak of guesses and probable signs of reprobation, since no certain signs of it are given, as there are for election. The question here is: Is reprobation not certain for the reprobate in this life, as election is certain? It is not. Hear here the severe exactor of piety and theologian in doctrine and life, Georgius Martonfalvi of Transylvania, the eagle among the theologians of Hungary, my only teacher in theology throughout my whole life in my homeland, writing thus about the uncertainty of reprobation in his most learned sermon: It is certain that Christ did not plead the cause of all equally before God, nor prayed for the world; yet God has wished to reserve the certainty of reprobation to himself, and, being merciful and compassionate, he has not wished to signify it even to the reprobate themselves. For if the reprobate knew it, they would have become more savage and cruel than the devils themselves; they would have overthrown the world until now, they would have despaired, they would have committed every outrage, and the elect themselves, because of their fierceness, would have been compelled to leave the world. Thus perhaps one of the chief reasons why God wished to conceal this is the elect, on whose account, as Christ the Lord testifies, the days of distress and affliction are shortened. And even if reprobation in this life were certain to the reprobate, it would come about either from the sin against the Holy Spirit, which falls only upon the reprobate, though not upon all of them; or from the opposites of those signs by which the elect are certain of their election; or from despair of the divine mercy. But the sin against the Holy Spirit cannot be a certain sign of reprobation for them, unless they also know that they have fallen into that sin, which none of the reprobate ever confesses about himself, since all men, and the reprobate too, are of such a disposition that they do not think ill of themselves. Nor can it be from the opposites of those signs by which the elect are made certain of their election, because all those things are common to the elect who are not yet regenerate and who are to be brought to the Church at a certain time. And as for a cause of despair concerning the grace and mercy of God, none of the reprobate can have such a cause in this life, unless it is clear to him that God does not wish him to be a partaker of his grace; and since this is rarely or never clear to anyone by ordinary means before the end of this life, therefore none of the reprobate can despair of the mercy of God. But if someone says that we shall below try carefully to prove the certainty of election, and consequently of reprobation, from a practical syllogism, since the opposites have opposite consequences, we reply: that logical rule has not so much as appeared in a dream concerning election and reprobation; therefore we do not acknowledge it as a norm of certainty, but order it to be banished from here. To the matter we say: he who finds in himself the opposites of the signs of election promises to amend his life, although he never does so, and thus he will remain uncertain of his reprobation in this life.

units.la: XXXV. Ratio hujus judicii est, quia, quamvis Deus novit, qui sint sui; nobis tamen consilia Dei sunt occulta, h.e. utut de electione nostra certi simus; de electione, tamen & reprobatione aliorum certi esse non possumus; quia consilium Dei de aliis ignoramus, quorum autem causas non novimus, eorum æqui judices haud esse quimus. Et certè, si φαινομένων in mundo rationes, qui in philosophando modesti sumus, dare nolumus, nisi eas nascentes, & orientes ab origine contemplemur, ut clarè, & distincte concipiamus; multò magis in occulto hoc, & infinito Dei consilio modestos nos esse oportet, ne ausu [?] vano mentem nostram putantes esse infinitam, temerè aliquid determinemus, & sic in istas difficultates incidamus, quibus nos extricare vix, aut nunquam valeamus. Occasione loci 2.Tim. 2:19. Novit Deus qui sunt sui. Quæritur, Novitne Deus, quot homines tandem salvi fient, & quinam sint singulariter illi homines? Affirm. Contra Socinianos, Pontif. Luth. 1.Q. Salvandorum nomina scripta sunt in cœlis, h.e. electi singulariter Deo curæ, cordique sunt, & ab ipso diliguntur, quod ut ad Apostolos in hypothesi agnitionis Christi, & fidei in ipsum; ita etiam ad omnes fideles pertinet; quemadmodum enim προγνωσία [?] & οἰκονομία [?] Christi circa Apostolos declarabat, eos non tantum terræ hujus scholæ esse discipulos; sed etiam matriculæ cœlestis Academiæ inscriptos: ita certè cura Christi Domini per Prophetas, ostendit electos Deo esse cordi, viam eorum ipsi esse notam, utpote ipso conscio, & authore suscepta & curatam. Unde etiam dicit, se suas nosse oves, & eas nominatim vocare. 2. Q. Electi dicuntur pars Jehovæ, & Jacob, h.e. dilecti Dei funiculus hæreditatis ejus Deut. 32. 9. Pars dicuntur propter separationem æternam, quâ plurimos reliquit, quos voluit, sibi assumsit, Psal.4:4·33:2. Funiculus dicuntur Jacob, q. ut suniculo partes hæreditatis distribuendæ mensurari solent: ita Deus electos suos suâ cognitione, veluti calamo mensorio determinavit. Neque otiosa hæc est Metaphora, quia Deus novit quos elegit Joh. 13: 18. quasi hæreditatem funiculo determinatam. Cum Scriptura mentionem faciat paucitatis electorum, Quæritur, Licetne quærere, An pauci sint qui salventur? Consessio exemplo Christi Salvatoris negat; qui Luc. 13:23. interroganti: an pauci sint qui salventur? non respondet; sed officii sui ipsum admonet; ut, relictâ curiosâ istâ quæstione, contendat ingredi per portam arctam h.e. ut Confessio explicat; Vestrum (sicut neque nostrum) non est, de his curiosius inquirere; sed magis anniti, ut per rectam viam cœlum ingrediamini, h.e. ut ego interpretor, via salutis etiam sine iis curiosis quæstionibus satis strictâ, satis difficilis est, & per multas angustias per eam ad vitam ingredi oportet; non igitur opus est pluribus implicari difficultatibus. Eos autem, qui tales curiosas quæstiones urgent, pluribus difficultatibus eos luctari necesse est. לאדני אלהינו הרחמים והסליחות לנו בשת הפנים
units.tr: XXXV. The reason for this judgment is that, although God knows who are his own, the counsels of God are hidden from us; that is, however certain we may be of our own election, we cannot be certain of the election and reprobation of others, because we do not know the counsel of God concerning others, and those whose causes we do not know we cannot be fair judges of. Indeed, if we who are modest in philosophy are unwilling to give reasons for the phenomena [φαινομένων] in the world unless we contemplate them as they arise and emerge from their origin, so that we may conceive them clearly and distinctly, much more ought we to be modest in this hidden and infinite counsel of God, lest, supposing our mind to be infinite through vain daring, we rashly determine something and so fall into those difficulties from which we can scarcely or never extricate ourselves. On the occasion of the passage 2 Tim. 2:19: The Lord knows those who are his own. The question is: Does God know how many men will at last be saved, and who in particular those men are? Yes. Against the Socinians, the Papists and the Lutherans, the first question: The names of those to be saved are written in heaven; that is, the elect are individually a concern and cherished by God, and are loved by him. As this applies to the Apostles under the hypothesis of recognition of Christ and faith in him, so it applies also to all the faithful; for just as the foreknowledge [προγνωσία] and the economy [οἰκονομία] of Christ concerning the Apostles showed that they were not merely disciples of this earthly school, but were also enrolled in the register of the heavenly academy, so surely the care of Christ the Lord, shown through the Prophets, shows that the elect are dear to God, and that their way is known to him, as one who is aware of and the author of what he has undertaken and looks after.
