Hence he also says that he knows his sheep and calls them by name. 2. Question: the elect are called the portion of Jehovah and Jacob; that is, the beloved cord of his inheritance, Deut. 32:9. They are called a portion because of the eternal separation by which he left out very many whom he did not wish, and took to himself those whom he wished (Ps. 4:4; 33:2). They are called the cord of Jacob, because, as portions of an inheritance to be distributed are usually measured by a cord, so God has determined his elect by his knowledge, as if with a measuring reed. Nor is this metaphor idle, because God knows whom he has chosen (John 13:18), as an inheritance is determined by a cord. Since Scripture makes mention of the fewness of the elect, the question is: Is it lawful to ask whether few are saved? The Confession, following the example of Christ the Saviour, denies it. He, in Luke 13:23, does not answer the one asking whether few are saved, but reminds him of his duty, so that, leaving aside that curious question, he should strive to enter through the narrow door; that is, as the Confession explains: it is not yours (as neither is it ours) to inquire too curiously into these things, but rather to strive that you may enter heaven by the right way. That is, as I interpret it: the way of salvation, even without those curious questions, is narrow enough and difficult enough, and one must enter life through many straits; there is therefore no need to entangle oneself in further difficulties. Those, however, who press such curious questions must necessarily struggle with more difficulties. To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness; to us shame of face [לאדני אלהינו הרחמים והסליחות לנו בשת הפנים].

units.la: Corollaria ex corpore disputationis petita.
units.tr: Corollaries drawn from the body of the disputation.

units.la: 1. Confessio Helvetica arguit primos Evangelii restauratores, unicè Scripturæ adhæsisse, & distinctionibus Scholasticorum minimè usos esse. Ergo.
units.tr: 1. The Helvetic Confession shows that the first restorers of the Gospel adhered solely to Scripture and made little use of the distinctions of the Scholastics. Therefore.

units.la: 1. Ecclesia reformata habet splendidissimum speculum eas cavendi.
units.tr: 1. The Reformed Church has a most splendid mirror for avoiding them.

units.la: 2. Doctores Ecclesiæ Reformatæ, qui inhiant hodie distinctionibus Scholasticorum, non insistunt vestigiis primorum Evangelii restauratorum.
units.tr: 2. The teachers of the Reformed Church who today dote on the distinctions of the Scholastics do not walk in the footsteps of the first restorers of the Gospel.

units.la: 3. Non immeritò Magnus hodie Theologus Scripturarius Franciscus Burmannus in Synopsi Oeconomiæ fœderum Dei cap. 2. §. 48. ita nobiscum queritur: Dolendum, terminos hosce obscuros, abusu contaminatos, parientes litem, non recipientes verba Scripturæ, & ea non suggerentes; sed qui potius causa sunt, ut eorum oblivisçamur, illam Theologiam ex ipsorum protestantium Scholis, contra Primorum Reformatorum (NB) exemplum, & institutum, non satis eliminari; imò & postliminio quasi reduci, cùm in Theologia positiva, ubi agendum est vocibus Scripturæ, vix ullum habeat usum; & in controversiis cum adversariis tractandis, si quod verborum præstet compendium, rebus tamen ipsis magis obstaculo, quàm adjumento sit.
units.tr: 3. Not without reason does the great Scripture-based theologian Franciscus Burmannus complain with us today, in his Synopsis of the Economy of God's Covenants, chapter 2, §48, as follows: "It is to be lamented that these obscure terms, tainted by abuse, which breed strife, which do not receive the words of Scripture and do not suggest them, are not sufficiently eliminated from the schools of the Protestants themselves; they are rather the cause of our forgetting that theology, contrary to the example and practice of the first Reformers (NB). Indeed, they are, as it were, brought back by the right of return, since they have hardly any use in positive theology, where we must deal in the words of Scripture; and in handling controversies with adversaries, if they offer some shortcut in words, they are nonetheless more of a hindrance than a help to the things themselves."

units.la: 11. Scriptura est verbum Dei. Ergo verbum vitæ æternæ, ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: II. Scripture is the Word of God. Therefore it is the word of eternal life, leading to eternal life.

units.la: III. Distinctiones Scholasticorum nihil aliud sunt in S. Sanctâ Theologiâ, quàm fumus ex puteo abyssi emissus ad obscurandum Solem, h.e. simplicem Scripturæ veritatem. Ergo
units.tr: III. The distinctions of the Scholastics are nothing else in holy Theology than smoke sent up from the pit of the abyss to darken the Sun, that is, the simple truth of Scripture. Therefore

units.la: 1. Quamdiu Ecclesia Reformata loquitur distinctiones Scholasticorum, tamdiu non loquitur purè verbum Dei.
units.tr: 1. As long as the Reformed Church speaks the distinctions of the Scholastics, so long it does not speak the pure Word of God.

units.la: 2. Quorundam Doctorum Ecclesia Reformata refugium, [?]ficulneum folium, πρῶτον ψευδῶς, pro necessitate distinctionum Scholasticarum: propter adversarios: Deo, Scripturæ, & primis Evangelii restauratoribus injuriosum est: Deo; quia Christus & Apostoli suos adversarios ad Scripturam, ad legem, ad testimonium, ad Mosen, ad Prophetas provocarunt. Scripturæ; quia sicut diabolus calumniator est operum Dei, ita distinctiones Scholasticorum Scripturæ. Primis Evangelii restauratoribus; q. illis, ad debellandum suos hostes, spiritualia Scripturæ arma sufficiebant.
units.tr: 2. To take refuge in the distinctions of the Scholastics, as some teachers of the Reformed Church do, is a fig-leaf, [first falsely] [πρῶτον ψευδῶς], for the necessity of such distinctions on account of adversaries. It is injurious to God, to Scripture, and to the first restorers of the Gospel. To God, because Christ and the Apostles summoned their adversaries to Scripture, to the law, to the testimony, to Moses, and to the Prophets. To Scripture, because just as the devil is the calumniator of the works of God, so the distinctions of the Scholastics are of Scripture. To the first restorers of the Gospel, for whom the spiritual weapons of Scripture sufficed to overcome their enemies.

units.la: 3. Quamdiu in Ecclesia verbum hominum auditur, tamdiu illud Iesaia: Erunt filii vestri discipuli Dei, non verificatur.
units.tr: 3. As long as the words of men are heard in the Church, so long that saying of Isaiah, "Your sons shall be disciples of God," is not fulfilled.

units.la: 4. Non potest Doctor Ecclesiæ Reformatæ discipulum Iesu Christi, sua fidei commissum, bona conscientia docere, nisi verbum Dei; Non enim homines audiendos & recipiendos suadere debet; sed Deum, Gal. 1:10.
units.tr: 4. A teacher of the Reformed Church cannot, with a good conscience, teach the disciples of Jesus Christ, entrusted to his faith, anything but the Word of God; for he ought not to persuade them to hear and receive men, but God. Gal. 1:10.

units.la: 5. Scholastica Theologia, Dilecta illa Pontificiorum Helena (ut Magnus, in doctiss. differ. sua de Scholastica Theologia, amat loqui Heideggerus,) est χάραγμα bestiæ, h. e. populi carnalis, justitiam Dei ignorantis, regnum Dei spirituale in regnum hominis carnale transmutantis & Christo mentientis.
units.tr: 5. Scholastic Theology, that beloved Helen of the Papists (as the great Heidegger, in his most learned dissertation on Scholastic Theology, likes to call her), is the mark [χάραγμα] of the beast, that is, of the carnal people, who are ignorant of the righteousness of God, who transform the spiritual kingdom of God into a carnal kingdom of man, and who lie against Christ.

units.la: IV. Quicunque in S. Sancta Scriptura terminis Scholasticis utitur, ille etiam abusui terminorum Scripturæ velificatur.
units.tr: IV. Whoever uses Scholastic terms in holy Scripture also gives sail to the abuse of the terms of Scripture.

units.la: V. Non ergo miramur Theologos Scholasticos abuti verbis Scripturæ, & ea irreverenter tractare; quâ enim impudentiâ istos terminos in scriptura spargunt; eâdem phrases Scripturæ rebus prophanis applicare non erubescunt.
units.tr: V. We are therefore not surprised that Scholastic theologians abuse the words of Scripture and handle them irreverently; for with what shamelessness they scatter these terms through Scripture, with the same impudence they are not ashamed to apply the phrases of Scripture to profane matters.

units.la: VI. Ecclesia Reformata est virgo, unicè Iesu Christo desponsata.
units.tr: VI. The Reformed Church is a virgin, betrothed to Jesus Christ alone.

units.la: VII. Babylon spiritualis est corrivalis magnæ meretricis.
units.tr: VII. Spiritual Babylon is the rival of the great harlot.

units.la: VIII. Distinctiones Scholasticæ sunt magnæ ejusdem meretricis nugæ & garrulitates; meretrix enim ut nugivendula, ita garrula est. Ergo,
units.tr: VIII. The Scholastic distinctions are the trifles and chatter of that same harlot; for the harlot, being a seller of trifles, is also garrulous. Therefore,

units.la: 1. Ecclesia Reformata, ut virgo, nullam potest cum ea habere communionem; non enim decet virginem commercium habere cum meretrice.
units.tr: 1. The Reformed Church, as a virgin, can have no communion with them; for it is not fitting for a virgin to have dealings with a harlot.

units.la: 2. Non potest Ecclesia Reformata, ut virgo, loqui verba, nisi sponsi, cui desponsata est, adeóque bonâ conscientiâ distinctiones Scholasticorum, q. non docet virginem loqui verba meretricum.
units.tr: 2. The Reformed Church, as a virgin, cannot speak any words except those of her Bridegroom, to whom she is betrothed, and therefore cannot with a good conscience teach the distinctions of the Scholastics, since this would not be teaching the virgin to speak the words of harlots.

units.la: 3. Prout Ecclesia Reformata nuditatem magnæ meretricis semel toti mundo detexit: Ita distinctiones Scholasticas, tanquam ejusdem meretricis nugas, & garrulitates, bonâ conscientiâ, posteandem meretricem ablegare tenetur.
units.tr: 3. Just as the Reformed Church has once for all exposed the nakedness of the great harlot to the whole world, so it is bound, with a good conscience, to send away the Scholastic distinctions, as the trifles and chatter of that same harlot, to that harlot afterwards.

units.la: FINIS
units.tr: FINIS
